claims.trigger: A `<Form validateOn="submit" validate={{ email: v => v ? undefined : 'Required' }} defaultValues={{ email: '' }}>` whose bound Input is focused and then blurred without any submit.
claims.wrongResult: The field's validator runs on that first blur and its error lands in the error map, so the error `<Message>` renders and `valid` flips false before the form is ever submitted.
claims.contract: `ValidateOn` TSDoc in the same file: "When the reducer runs validators: on a field's first blur (`'touched'`), on every keystroke (`'change'`), or only on submit (`'submit'`)."
claims.evidence: form-reducer.ts: the 'set-value' case guards the submit mode (lines 150-152, `if (action.validateOn === 'submit') return { ...state, values: nextValues }`), but the 'set-touched' case (lines 163-181) calls `runValidators(action.validate, state.values, nextTouched, action.validateOn, [action.name])` with a `fields` argument. In `runValidators`, `forced = fields !== undefined` (line 62) and the gate is `if (forced || validateOn === 'change' || (validateOn === 'touched' && touched[key]))` (line 73), so the forced path ignores `validateOn` entirely. Trace: Input onBlur -> useFormText.onBlur (use-form-text.ts line 52) -> field.setTouched() -> useFormReducer.setTouched (use-form-reducer.ts lines 186-191) -> dispatch 'set-touched' -> validator runs. Suspected severity: medium (the 'submit' mode is indistinguishable from 'touched' for every field the user visits). Fix: mirror the 'set-value' guard — when `action.validateOn === 'submit'`, return `{ ...state, touched: nextTouched }` without calling `runValidators`.

claims.trigger: `<CurrencyInput className="w-40" />` — any call site that passes `className`.
claims.wrongResult: The component's own `tabular-nums` class is replaced rather than merged, so the rendered input loses tabular figures and the digits jitter horizontally as the user types.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Presentational attributes stay overridable: … `className` merges through `cn`."
claims.evidence: currency-input.tsx: `className` is absent from the destructure (lines 47-62) so it stays inside `...props`; the element sets `className="tabular-nums"` at line 103 and then spreads `{...props}` at line 142, so the consumer value wins outright. `className` is part of `InputProps` (input.tsx line 26) and is not in the `Omit` list at lines 13-16, so this is reachable from typed call sites. Sibling precedent that does merge: number-input.tsx line 144 (`className={cn(k.number, className)}`) and search-input.tsx line 148. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: destructure `className` and render `className={cn('tabular-nums', className)}`.

claims.trigger: Typing a 17-or-more-digit amount (e.g. `12345678901234567`) into a `<CurrencyInput>`.
claims.wrongResult: The field displays — and `onValueChange` emits — a different number from the one typed (the trailing digits are rewritten, e.g. the final `7` becomes `8`), so the amount silently changes under the user.
claims.evidence: currency-input-utilities.ts: `groupIntegerPart` (lines 45-62) converts the digit string with `const n = Number(trimmed)` (line 50) and re-renders it through `n.toLocaleString(...)` (lines 56-60); above 2^53 that round trip is lossy. `formatEditing` calls it on every keystroke (line 78), and CurrencyInput commits the result to `editingText` and parses it back with `parseEditing` (currency-input.tsx lines 110-127), so both the display and the emitted number carry the corrupted digits. Suspected severity: low (large-amount fields only, but silent). Fix: group the digit string directly (insert the separator every three characters from the right) instead of routing it through `Number`.
claims.contract: `groupIntegerPart`'s own comment: "Strips redundant leading zeros and applies locale digit grouping" — grouping is a presentation step and must not alter the digits; CurrencyInput's TSDoc likewise promises it "Emits a `number` via `onValueChange` while displaying grouped digits".

claims.trigger: A controlled masked control, e.g. `<PhoneInput value="5551234567" onValueChange={setPhone} />` or `<MaskInput value="4111111111111111" format={…} />`.
claims.wrongResult: The field renders the raw unformatted string (`5551234567`) instead of the masked form (`(555) 123-4567`); the mask only appears after the user edits the field.
claims.contract: `useMaskInput` TSDoc: "Applies `format` to the seed and to every subsequent change" and "@returns The `value` (formatted, never `undefined`)".
claims.evidence: use-mask-input.ts lines 52-66: only `defaultValue` is passed through `format` (line 59); `value` is handed to `useFormValue` untouched and returned as `current ?? ''` (line 66). In use-form-value.ts, `bound` is false whenever `value !== undefined` (line 51), so `useControllable` echoes the raw prop back (use-controllable.ts line 34). Every masked control inherits this: mask-input.tsx line 59, credit-card-input.tsx line 80, credit-card-input-cvv.tsx line 121, credit-card-input-expiry.tsx line 96, phone-input.tsx, zipcode-input.tsx. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: format the controlled prop as well — pass `value: value !== undefined ? format(value) : value` into `useFormValue`.

claims.trigger: `<Field><Label>Shipping address</Label><AddressInput /></Field>` with no explicit `aria-label`.
claims.wrongResult: The combobox's accessible name is the placeholder text ("Enter an address") instead of the field's Label, because an `aria-label` is set unconditionally and outranks the `<label>` association in the accessible-name computation.
claims.contract: AddressInput TSDoc @remarks: "Reads enclosing Density/Control context for disabled state and accessible name (falls back to `placeholder`)."
claims.evidence: address-input.tsx: `useControl()` is read only for `disabled` (line 118); `aria-label={ariaLabel ?? placeholder}` is passed unconditionally at line 137, so the control never consults `control?.labelledBy` as the TSDoc claims. The house pattern is in the same scope: credit-card-input-cvv.tsx line 117 `aria-label={ariaLabel ?? (control?.labelledBy ? undefined : 'Security code')}` with the comment "defaults an aria-label, yielding to a registered Field <Label>", and credit-card-input-expiry.tsx line 92. Suspected severity: medium (WCAG 2.5.3 / 4.1.2 — the visible label and the spoken name diverge). Fix: `aria-label={ariaLabel ?? (control?.labelledBy ? undefined : placeholder)}`.

claims.trigger: `<Field><Label>Skills</Label><TagInput /></Field>` with no `placeholder`.
claims.wrongResult: The inner text input announces as "Add tags" rather than "Skills": the hard-coded `aria-label` overrides the Label the Field registered.
claims.contract: The family contract stated in the sibling's TSDoc comment (credit-card-input-cvv.tsx): "The placeholder is not a programmatic name (WCAG 3.3.2 / 4.1.2); defaults an aria-label, yielding to a registered Field <Label>."
claims.evidence: tag-input.tsx line 239: `aria-label={placeholder ?? 'Add tags'}` is passed to `Input` unconditionally, and the component never reads `useControl()` (no import of the control context in this file at all, lines 1-19 — only `ControlSize` as a type). Because `aria-label` outranks a `<label for>` association, the Field's `<Label>` text is discarded. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: read `useControl()` and fall back to `undefined` when `control?.labelledBy` is set, as the credit-card fields do.

claims.trigger: `<Message name="email" all data-testid="email-errors" />` inside a Form whose `email` field holds two or more errors.
claims.wrongResult:
The rendered `
    ` carries no `data-testid` (nor any other passed native attribute or handler), while the same component with a single error renders them on the `

    ` — so the attribute silently disappears when a second error arrives.
claims.contract: `MessageProps` is declared as `{ … } & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'p'>, 'className' | 'name'>`, i.e. the native attribute surface is part of the component's public props.
claims.evidence: message.tsx: the multi-error branch at lines 123-141 builds the `<ul>` with only `data-slot`, `data-severity`, `id`, `role` and `className` and never spreads `{...props}`; the single-message branch at lines 145-156 does spread it (line 152). The branch is entered only when `isFormBoundError && issues && all && issues.length > 1` (line 123), so the prop loss is data-dependent. Suspected severity: low-medium (breaks test hooks and any aria-* the caller adds, only once a second error exists). Fix: spread `{...props}` on the `<ul>` as well.

claims.trigger: `<Message role="note">Something went wrong</Message>`.
claims.wrongResult: The consumer prop replaces the component's `role="alert"`, so the validation text is no longer an assertive live region and assistive tech never announces it.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state, and the resolved wiring of the §7.2 binding cascade — are written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't drop a row out of roving, turn a button into a form submit, or clobber a bound field".
claims.evidence:
message.tsx lines 145-153: the `

` writes `role={role}` (line 151, resolved at line 121 to `alert` for the error severity) before `{...props}` (line 152), and `role` is not destructured out of `props` (lines 74-82) — `MessageProps` includes the native `

` attributes (line 22), so `role` is a typed, reachable prop. Suspected severity: low (needs a caller to pass `role`, but the attribute is exactly the one §3.9 names). Fix: move `role` (and `data-severity`) after the spread in both return branches.

claims.trigger: `<Form defaultValues={{ email: '' }}><Input name="email" defaultValue="me@example.com" /></Form>`.
claims.wrongResult: The `<input>` receives both the bound `value` and the stray `defaultValue`, so React logs the "contains an input of type text with both value and defaultValue props" error and the field is left in the mixed controlled/uncontrolled state that warning describes.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §7.2: "A bound field ignores the control's `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked`; `Form.defaultValues` is the single source of truth."
claims.evidence: input.tsx: `defaultValue` is not destructured (lines 43-65) so it rides in `...rest` and is spread onto the element at line 112, next to the resolved `value={valueState.value}` at line 103. `useInputValue` returns the bound field's string whenever `value === undefined && binding !== undefined` (use-input-value.ts lines 47-52), so the pair is present exactly in the bound case §7.2 describes. Suspected severity: low-medium (dev-time console error; test suites that fail on console.error break). Fix: destructure `defaultValue` in `Input` and forward it only when the control resolves to uncontrolled.

claims.trigger: `<Form defaultValues={{ bio: '' }}><Textarea name="bio" defaultValue="seed" /></Form>`.
claims.wrongResult: The `<textarea>` gets the bound `value` and the stray `defaultValue` together, producing React's "both value and defaultValue props" error and an inconsistent initial render.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §7.2: "A bound field ignores the control's `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked`; `Form.defaultValues` is the single source of truth."
claims.evidence: textarea.tsx: the destructure (lines 35-56) omits `defaultValue`, so it stays in `...rest` and is spread at line 133 alongside `controlProps.value` (line 94), which `useInputValue` fills from the bound field. Same mechanism as the Input case; `Textarea` shares the cascade hook (line 59). Suspected severity: low-medium. Fix: destructure `defaultValue` and pass it only when `valueState.value === undefined`.

claims.trigger: `<Control size="sm"><Input /><Input /></Control>` — one Control wrapping more than one control-aware descendant.
claims.wrongResult: Both inputs render the same `id` attribute, so the document holds duplicate ids and any label or `aria-describedby` reference resolves to the first field only.
claims.contract: Control TSDoc: "Form-field context provider: generates a stable id and broadcasts `autoComplete`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `severity`, `size`, and `variant` to control-aware descendants (input, textarea, switch, listbox, combobox, datepicker, checkbox, radio)."
claims.evidence: control.tsx: one `useIdScope` per Control (line 55) and the single `id: scope.id` published in the context value (line 73). Every field takes it verbatim — use-control-props.ts line 89 `id: input.id ?? control?.id` — and Input then feeds that straight into its own scope (input.tsx lines 83, 95). The a11y ids derived in `useA11yControl(scope.id)` (control.tsx line 69) are likewise shared, so a single `<Label>`/`<Description>` describes every field in the scope. Suspected severity: medium (duplicate ids, mis-targeted label clicks). Fix: broadcast the id only for a single-control scope (as `Field`/`ControlField` do, control-field.tsx lines 28-32), or have each field derive a per-instance id from the scope instead of adopting it.

claims.trigger: `<Control required><Control size="sm"><Input /></Control></Control>` — an inner Control opened only to change size or variant.
claims.wrongResult: The inner Control publishes `required: undefined`, so the nested input loses the ancestor's required state (no `required` attribute, no required styling), while the same nesting through `<Field>` keeps it.
claims.contract: Control TSDoc: "Form-field context provider: generates a stable id and broadcasts `autoComplete`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `severity`, `size`, and `variant` to control-aware descendants … Nests: `disabled` / `readOnly` cascade through inner Controls, `severity` / `size` / `variant` inherit unless overridden."
claims.evidence: control.tsx lines 57-67 merge every other axis with the parent (`mergedDisabled`, `mergedReadOnly`, `mergedSeverity`, `mergedSize`, `mergedVariant`, `mergedAutoComplete`) but line 76 publishes the bare `required` prop with no parent fallback. The field-wrapper twin does inherit it: use-control-field-context.ts line 53 `required: parent?.required`. Suspected severity: low. Fix: `required: required ?? parent?.required` and add it to the memo dependency list.

claims.trigger: Importing `classifyTokens` or `TokenBatch` from the `ui/tag-input` barrel (the documented public surface), or running the internal-surface rule over the components layer.
claims.wrongResult: A symbol whose own doccomment declares it `@internal` is package-public through the barrel, so the surface docs and any doc tooling see the same symbol as both public and internal.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §12.1: "`@internal` on a documented helper that no barrel re-exports — the tag and a barrel entry are mutually exclusive, pinned by `internal-barrel-boundary.test.ts`."
claims.evidence: tag-input-utilities.ts carries `@internal` on `TokenBatch` (doccomment ending line 63, declaration line 65) and on `classifyTokens` (doccomment ending line 87, declaration line 88), while tag-input/index.ts line 7 re-exports both: `export { classifyTokens, splitTokens, type TokenBatch } from './tag-input-utilities'`. The barrel's own comment (index.ts lines 2-6) argues the export is deliberate, so the stale tags are the defect. The existing gate misses it: internal-barrel-boundary.test.ts line 20 scans `LAYERS = ['core','hooks','layouts','primitives','providers','types','utilities']` and never walks `components`. Suspected severity: low. Fix: drop the `@internal` tag from `classifyTokens` and `TokenBatch` (keep it on `hasSeparator` / `describeBatch`, which stay unbarrelled).

claims.trigger: Clearing a `<NumberInput onValueChange={v => …} />` (select-all + Delete) and testing the argument with `v === undefined`.
claims.wrongResult: The callback receives `null`, not `undefined`, so a consumer following the documented contract never detects the cleared state.
claims.contract: NumberInput TSDoc on the prop: "Fires with the parsed value, or `undefined` when the field is cleared."
claims.evidence: number-input.tsx line 28 documents `undefined` while the signature on line 29 is `(value: number | null) => void`; the clear path calls `setCurrent(undefined)` (line 106) which reaches `useControllable`'s setter, and that normalizes and emits `onValueChangeRef.current?.(normalized ?? null)` (use-controllable.ts line 67, per CONVENTIONS §7.3). Suspected severity: low (documentation contradicts the type and the runtime value). Fix: reword the prop doc to "or `null` once it is cleared", matching use-form-value.ts line 12.

claims.trigger: `<PasswordConfirm warning="Passwords do not match">` where the user types two different passwords, causing the warning to appear for the first time.
claims.wrongResult: The `role="status"` element is inserted into the DOM already carrying its text, so the mismatch is not reliably announced — assistive tech watches live regions that existed before the content changed.
claims.contract: `useA11yLiveRegion` TSDoc: "Props for a live region the consumer fills with children … For imperative, no-visible-home announcements use `announce` / `useA11yAnnouncements` instead."
claims.evidence:
password-confirm.tsx: the live-region bag is built at line 69 but the element it belongs to is mounted only inside `{status === 'warning' && warning && !confirmHasFormError && (…)}` (lines 75-79), so the region and its text appear in the same commit. The sibling in this scope keeps the region permanently mounted and swaps only its children: password-strength.tsx line 100 `
{label}
`. Suspected severity: low-medium (WCAG 4.1.3). Fix: render the wrapper unconditionally with the id and live-region props, and render the `` child conditionally.

claims.trigger: Render `<LocaleProvider locale="en-GB"><DatePicker input onValueChange={fn} /></LocaleProvider>` and type `10062026` into the field.
claims.wrongResult: The field masks and parses month-first (`10/06/2026` read as 6 October) instead of the day-first order the ambient locale asks for, so the typed date disagrees with the Monday-first calendar the same picker opens. The same happens to the relative variant's Start/End fields, which are `input`-mode pickers with no `format`.
claims.contract: `date-input.tsx` states the intent for the locale default: "Field order follows the ambient locale unless the caller pins it, so the masked field agrees with the Calendar it pairs with inside a DatePicker." `DateInputProps.format` documents `@defaultValue The layout matching the ambient <LocaleProvider> locale — 'DD/MM/YYYY' for a day-first locale, 'YYYY-MM-DD' for a year-first one, else 'MM/DD/YYYY'.` The sibling test `date-input.test.tsx` pins it: "masks a typed date day-first under a day-first locale … The field previously masked month-first whatever the locale, so this entry read as October."
claims.evidence: date-picker.tsx:244 destructures `format = 'MM/DD/YYYY'` and line 320 passes `format={format}` unconditionally to `<DateInput>`. Because the prop is always present (never `undefined`), `resolveDateInputFormat(formatProp, ambient.locale, …)` in date-input-utilities.ts:69 takes the `format ?? localeDateInputFormat(locale)` short branch and `localeDateInputFormat` never runs. date-picker-relative.tsx:160 and :172 mount `<DatePicker input …>` with no `format`, inheriting the same hard default. Severity: high — a silent mis-parse of user-entered dates in every non-`MM/DD/YYYY` locale, exactly the regression the DateInput locale work fixed. Fix: drop the `'MM/DD/YYYY'` default in `DatePickerSingle` and forward `format={props.format}` (undefined-passthrough) so DateInput's own locale resolution runs; update `DatePickerSingleProps.format`'s `@defaultValue` to match.

claims.trigger: Render `<DatePicker input readOnly value={new Date(2026, 5, 15)} onValueChange={fn} />` and type digits into the field, or click its clear button.
claims.wrongResult: The text field stays editable and clearable: typing rewrites the masked text, `onValueChange` fires with a new `Date`, and the clear affordance renders and empties the value — a read-only picker changes its value.
claims.contract: `DatePickerBaseProps.readOnly`: "Keeps the trigger focusable and the value submitted, but blocks opening the calendar and changing the value."
claims.evidence: date-picker.tsx:325 passes `disabled={state.disabled}` to `<DateInput>` but never passes `readOnly`. `useDatePickerState` computes `resolvedReadOnly` (use-date-picker-state.ts:63) and does not return it, so the input branch has nothing to forward. Inside DateInput, `resolvedReadOnly = readOnly ?? control?.readOnly` (date-input.tsx:179) is therefore undefined outside a `<Control readOnly>`, so `dateInputSuffix` renders the clear button (date-input.tsx:325) and `<Input readOnly={undefined}>` leaves the native field editable. DateInput already honours `readOnly` correctly when given it, so the gap is purely the missing forward. Severity: high (data-integrity: a read-only field accepts edits). Fix: return `readOnly: resolvedReadOnly` from `useDatePickerState` and pass `readOnly={state.readOnly}` to `<DateInput>`.

claims.trigger: Render `<Form defaultValues={{ due: null }} resolver={schemaRejectingEmpty}><DatePicker input name="due" /></Form>` (no `<Field severity>`), submit to produce a field error, then read the input's ARIA state. Compare with the same picker without `input`.
claims.wrongResult: The typed field carries no `aria-invalid` and no invalid chrome, while the button-trigger form of the same picker does. The bound Form field's error state is computed and then discarded, so a keyboard/AT user gets no programmatic signal that the field failed validation.
claims.contract: `useDatePickerState` documents its return as "Trigger props (`triggerId`, `displayValue`, `disabled`, `invalid`, …)", and `Input`'s TSDoc states "`invalid` OR's the prop, the bound field, and any ambient Control error" — the bound field here is the picker's, not the input's.
claims.evidence: use-date-picker-state.ts:267 returns `invalid: control?.severity === 'error' || fieldInvalid` and `required: control?.required`; `fieldInvalid` comes from `useFormValue(name, …)` on the *picker's* name. date-picker.tsx:364-366 forwards both to `<DatePickerTrigger>` in the button branch, but the `input` branch (lines 316-343) forwards neither. `<DateInput>` receives no `name`, so its own `useInputValue`/`useFormText` binding is absent (`bound === false` because `value` is always the defined `text` string), and `<Field>` only broadcasts a caller-supplied `severity` (field.tsx:46), never a Form error. Severity: medium (WCAG 3.3.1 signalling gap, single-variant asymmetry). Fix: pass `invalid={state.invalid}` and `required={state.required}` to `<DateInput>` in the `input` branch.

claims.trigger: Render `<DatePicker readOnly clearable value={new Date(2026, 5, 15)} onValueChange={fn} />` and click the clear (✕) button the trigger renders beside the value.
claims.wrongResult: The value is cleared and `onValueChange(null)` fires on a read-only picker. The same hook also lets a caller-controlled `open` bypass the guard entirely: `<DatePicker readOnly open value={…} />` renders the dialog and every day cell commits a new value.
claims.contract: `DatePickerBaseProps.readOnly`: "Keeps the trigger focusable and the value submitted, but blocks opening the calendar and changing the value." The hook's own comment narrows it to opening only: "readOnly keeps the trigger focusable and the value submitted but blocks every open path".
claims.evidence: use-date-picker-state.ts:63 computes `resolvedReadOnly`, and lines 87-94 apply it only inside `setOpen`. `handleClear` (154-158) and `handleSelect` (143-152) call `setValue` unguarded, and the hook returns `onClear: handleClear` (271) plus `hasValue` (270) with no read-only flag. date-picker-trigger.tsx:99 gates the clear button on `clearable && hasValue && !disabled` — `readOnly` is not a prop it ever receives. The `open` bypass follows from `useControllable` (use-controllable.ts:32-34): a defined `value` prop wins per render, so `open` stays true whatever `setOpen` refuses. The existing test only pins "readOnly blocks opening but keeps the trigger focusable" (date-picker.test.tsx:451). Severity: high. Fix: early-return from `handleClear`/`handleSelect` when `resolvedReadOnly`, and return `readOnly` so the trigger can drop the clear affordance.

claims.trigger: Render `<DatePicker range readOnly clearable value={[new Date(2026, 5, 1), new Date(2026, 5, 8)]} onValueChange={fn} />` and click the trigger's clear (✕) button.
claims.wrongResult: The committed `[Date, Date]` is cleared and `onValueChange(null)` fires despite `readOnly`. With a caller-controlled `open`, day clicks likewise commit a new range.
claims.contract: `DatePickerBaseProps.readOnly`: "Keeps the trigger focusable and the value submitted, but blocks opening the calendar and changing the value."
claims.evidence: use-date-picker-range-state.ts:61 computes `resolvedReadOnly` and lines 86-93 apply it only in `setOpen`. `handleClear` (157-161) calls `setValue(undefined)` and `handleSelect` (163-185) calls `setValue(range)` with no guard; the hook returns `onClear: handleClear` (265) and `calendar.onValueChange: handleSelect` (283). `DatePickerRange` wires `onClear={state.onClear}` and `hasValue={state.hasValue}` into `DatePickerTrigger` (date-picker-range.tsx:50-51), whose `showClear` never sees `readOnly`. Severity: high. Fix: guard both writers on `resolvedReadOnly` and expose the flag to the trigger.

claims.trigger: Render `<DatePicker relative readOnly clearable value={[{ from: d1, to: d2 }]} onValueChange={fn} />` and click the trigger's clear (✕) button; or render the same picker with a controlled `open` and click a preset row.
claims.wrongResult: The committed spans are cleared (or replaced by the clicked preset) and `onValueChange` fires, on a picker documented as read-only.
claims.contract: `DatePickerBaseProps.readOnly`: "Keeps the trigger focusable and the value submitted, but blocks opening the calendar and changing the value."
claims.evidence: use-date-picker-relative-state.ts:77 computes `resolvedReadOnly`; lines 110-117 apply it only in `setOpen`. `handleClear` (212-220), `togglePreset` (155-187) and `applyDraft` (265-285) all call `setValue` unguarded, and the hook returns `onClear: handleClear` (407) plus `togglePreset` (415). `date-picker-relative.tsx:85` wires `onClear={state.onClear}` into the trigger, whose `showClear` gate (date-picker-trigger.tsx:99) reads only `disabled`. `resolvedDisabled` is checked in `onTriggerKeyDown` (line 345) but `resolvedReadOnly` never is. Severity: high. Fix: guard the three writers on `resolvedReadOnly` and pass the flag to the trigger.

claims.trigger: On the 1st of any month, render `<DatePicker relative={{ multiple: true }} />`, click "Today", then click "This month", then click "Today" again to deselect it.
claims.wrongResult: Two committed spans exist but only the later preset reads as selected: the "Today" row loses its `aria-pressed="true"` and solid highlight, and clicking it a second time re-adds it instead of removing it, so the user cannot deselect it. Both trigger chips read "This month".
claims.contract: `DatePickerRelativeConfig.multiple`: "Allows more than one preset selected at once; the value becomes a {@link DatePickerRelativeValue} array instead of a single span." `togglePresetValue`: "Multi-select adds or removes the preset and rebuilds the result in preset order so chips stay stable and deduped."
claims.evidence: On the 1st, `today.resolve` yields `{from: startOfDay(now), to: startOfDay(now)}` (line 87) and `this-month.resolve` yields `{from: startOfMonth(now), to: startOfDay(now)}` (line 116) — the identical span. `selectedPresetIds` (204-221) maps every span through `matchRelativePreset`, which walks `[...preferredIds].reverse()` and returns the single most-recently-picked match (189-198). With `pickedIds = {today, this-month}` both spans resolve to `this-month`, so the returned Set has size 1. `togglePresetValue`'s multi branch (262-271) then rebuilds `next` from that under-reported Set, and `selected.has('today')` is false on the deselect click, so line 265 adds instead of deleting. `date-picker-relative.tsx:111` drives the row highlight from `state.selectedIds`. "This year" collides with "Today" the same way on 1 January. Severity: medium (reachable with the built-in presets on the 1st of a month; stuck, unremovable selection). Fix: have `selectedPresetIds` consume each preferred id at most once (or match per-span against the remaining unclaimed ids) so N colliding spans map to N distinct presets.

claims.trigger: Commit two spans that resolve to the same preset — e.g. on the 1st of a month pick "Today" and "This month" with `relative={{ multiple: true }}`, or hand the picker `value={[span, span]}` for one preset's span.
claims.wrongResult: Both chips get the identical React `key` (`preset-<id>`) and the identical label, so React logs a duplicate-key warning and the trigger shows the same chip twice instead of naming each committed span.
claims.contract: `RelativeChip`: "A rendered trigger chip: a stable React `key` plus its display label." `relativeChips`: "Trigger chips for the committed value, in selection order: a matched preset's label, or the formatted absolute range for a custom span."
claims.evidence: relativeChips (280-297) keys a matched span `preset-${preset.id}` with no positional component, while the custom branch correctly uses the index (`custom-${index}`). Two entries of `value` that match the same preset therefore collide. `date-picker-relative.tsx:58` renders `<Badge key={chip.key}>` straight from that key. Severity: low-medium (React key warning plus a misleading duplicate label; reachable with the default presets on the 1st of a month). Fix: include the index in the preset key, e.g. `preset-${index}-${preset.id}`.

claims.trigger: Open the calendar's month/year picker while the calendar shows June 2026, press "Next year" twice so the header reads 2028, then click the centre year label to enter the decade grid.
claims.wrongResult: The decade grid marks 2026 (the calendar's year) with `aria-selected="true"`, the solid variant and `data-selected` instead of the 2028 the picker was just showing; the open-focus seek for `[data-selected]` therefore seats focus on 2026, and when the stepped year falls outside the visible decade no cell is marked at all and focus drops to the grid's first cell.
claims.contract: `CalendarPickerState`: "the active grid, the year whose months are shown, and the year anchoring the visible decade. `pickerYear` and `decadeYear` track independently so paging the decade grid never disturbs the chosen month-year." `CalendarPickerAction`: "`showYears`/`showMonths` swap views (entering years re-anchors the decade on `pickerYear`)". `CalendarPickerGridCell`: "`selected` marks the active choice".
claims.evidence: use-calendar-picker.tsx:169 sets `selected: y === year` on each year cell, comparing against the calendar's `year` prop, while the view itself is anchored on `pickerYear` — `showYears` sets `decadeYear = state.pickerYear` (calendar-picker-reducer.ts:50), `decadeStart = Math.floor(decadeYear / 10) * 10` (line 90) and the centre label renders `pickerYear` (line 185). The month cells guard the same mismatch explicitly (`selected: i === month && pickerYear === year`, line 158), so the two views disagree. `focusPickerGrid` (102-112) queries `[data-selected]`, which `calendar-picker-grid.tsx:105` stamps via `dataAttr(cell.selected)` (`'' | undefined`), so the wrong cell — or none — takes focus. Severity: low-medium (a11y: wrong `aria-selected` and initial focus in the year grid). Fix: use `selected: y === pickerYear` and keep `current` for the today marker.

claims.trigger: Render `<Checkbox indeterminate />` and click it (or focus it and press Space).
claims.wrongResult: The browser clears the input's `indeterminate` DOM property on activation and nothing restores it, so assistive tech announces "checked"/"not checked" while the component still paints the Minus (mixed) glyph. The visual state and the accessibility state disagree from that click onward, for as long as the `indeterminate` prop stays `true`.
claims.contract: TSDoc on `CheckboxProps.indeterminate`: "Renders the partial tri-state: a minus glyph and `indeterminate` DOM property regardless of `checked`."
claims.evidence: checkbox.tsx:75-77 — `useLayoutEffect(() => { if (internalRef.current) internalRef.current.indeterminate = !!indeterminate }, [indeterminate])`. The dependency array is the prop alone, so the effect re-runs only when the prop itself changes. A user click mutates `input.indeterminate` to `false` natively (pre-click activation), and React never manages that property, so no re-render restores it. Line 84 `const Mark = indeterminate ? Minus : Check` keeps drawing the mixed glyph from the unchanged prop. Suspected severity: moderate (a11y state/visual divergence, WCAG 4.1.2). Fix: drop the dependency array so the sync runs on every commit, or add `resolvedChecked` to it and also re-assert the property inside `resolvedOnChange`.

claims.trigger: `<Form defaultValues={{ agree: true }}><Checkbox name="agree" defaultChecked={false} /></Form>`
claims.wrongResult: `defaultChecked` survives into the rest-props bag and is spread onto the same `<input>` that already carries the bound `checked`, so React renders both and logs the controlled/uncontrolled input error. The bound field does not ignore the control's `defaultChecked` as the cascade requires.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §7.2: "A bound field ignores the control's `defaultValue`/`defaultChecked`; `Form.defaultValues` is the single source of truth." CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state, and the resolved wiring of the §7.2 binding cascade — are written *after* `{...props}` … `switch.tsx` the cascade one."
claims.evidence: checkbox.tsx:32-47 destructures `checked` and `onChange` but not `defaultChecked`; lines 92-106 write `type`, `checked={resolvedChecked}`, `onChange={resolvedOnChange}`, `{...validation}` and `data-slot` BEFORE `{...props}` at line 105. Compare switch.tsx:32 (destructures `defaultChecked`), :118 (`{...props}` first) and :127 (`{...(isControlled ? { checked: on ?? false } : { defaultChecked: defaultChecked ?? false })}`), the precedent §3.9 names. Suspected severity: low-moderate (React console error plus a silently ignored consumer prop). Fix: destructure `defaultChecked`, apply it only when `resolvedChecked === undefined`, and move `{...props}` above the resolved wiring as Switch does.

claims.trigger: `<Form schema={…}><SignaturePad name="sig" /></Form>` — move the pointer over the canvas and out again, or release a press that began elsewhere over the canvas, without ever drawing a stroke.
claims.wrongResult: The bound Form field is marked touched even though no stroke was made, so touched-gated validation messages ("Signature is required") appear for a pad the user never drew on.
claims.contract: TSDoc on `useSignaturePadState`: "`commit` (stroke end) and `clear` both mark the bound field touched — the pad's analogue of blur."
claims.evidence: use-signature-pad-state.ts:136-140 — `const commit = useCallback(() => { commitStroke(); setTouched() }, [commitStroke, setTouched])`. `commitStroke` bails at use-signature-pad-drawing.ts:122 (`if (!drawingRef.current) return`), but `setTouched()` is outside that guard and always runs. signature-pad.tsx:151-153 wires `commit` to `onPointerUp`, `onPointerCancel` and `onPointerLeave`, and `pointerleave`/`pointerup` fire with no preceding stroke. Suspected severity: moderate (spurious validation errors on hover). Fix: have `commitStroke` return whether it committed, and call `setTouched()` only then.

claims.trigger: Press and drag a RangeSlider thumb with the mouse, release, then press ArrowRight.
claims.wrongResult: The thumb button never receives DOM focus, because `preventDefault()` on `pointerdown` suppresses the compatibility mousedown and its focus default and nothing focuses the thumb by hand. The arrow key goes to `<body>` and the value does not move; a pointer user who then reaches for the keyboard has no focused slider, and focus has been silently lost from the page.
claims.contract: TSDoc on the sibling `useColorDrag`, which this hook's own comment names as its model: "`onPointerDown` calls `preventDefault` and focuses `ref` synchronously, so the primary-button press doubles as the keyboard-focus path (WAI-ARIA slider)."
claims.evidence: use-range-pointer.ts:117-156 — `onPointerDown` calls `event.preventDefault()` (line 121) and `setPointerCapture` (line 123) but never focuses a thumb; the comment at lines 187-189 says the hook mirrors `use-color-drag.ts`, which does focus (use-color-drag.ts:62-65). range-slider.tsx:130-134 hangs the handlers on the root div, so the press that lands on a thumb `<button>` bubbles here and is defaulted away. Suspected severity: moderate (WCAG 2.4.3 / 2.1.1 keyboard reachability after a pointer interaction). Fix: after resolving the dragged thumb, call `thumbRefs[thumb].current?.focus()` as `useColorDrag` does.

claims.trigger: Right-click (or middle-click) anywhere on a RangeSlider track.
claims.wrongResult: The nearest thumb jumps to the pointer position and the range commits, firing `onValueChange` and writing the bound Form field, on a non-primary button press that should only open the context menu.
claims.contract: TSDoc on the sibling `useColorDrag`, whose guard this hook otherwise mirrors: "Non-primary buttons are ignored." (`if (disabled || event.button !== 0) return`).
claims.evidence: use-range-pointer.ts:117-156 — line 119 guards `disabled` only; there is no `event.button !== 0` test before `preventDefault()`, `setPointerCapture` and `update(thumb, raw)` at lines 121-153. Compare use-color-drag.ts:60. Suspected severity: low-moderate (unintended value mutation and a captured pointer on a secondary press). Fix: add `|| event.button !== 0` to the guard at line 119.

claims.trigger: `<Form schema={…}><RangeSlider name="budget" /></Form>` — drag or arrow a thumb, then move focus off the slider.
claims.wrongResult: The bound field is never marked touched, so a Form that gates its error messages on `touched` never renders the range's validation message, unlike every sibling control (Slider, Rating, Combobox, SignaturePad) in the same Form.
claims.contract: TSDoc on `FormValueResult.setTouched` (`use-form-value.ts`): "Marks the field touched; no-op outside a Form. Call from `onBlur`."
claims.evidence: range-slider.tsx:74 — `const { value: range, setValue: setRange } = useFormValue<[number, number]>(name, {…})` destructures only `value` and `setValue`; `setTouched` is never pulled out and the root div carries no `onBlur`. Compare slider.tsx:65-76 and :119-123 (`onBlur` calls `setTouched()`), rating.tsx:145 and :269. Suspected severity: low-moderate. Fix: destructure `setTouched` and call it from an `onBlur` on the root div (or from each thumb's blur).

claims.trigger: `<Form schema={…}><RangeSlider name="budget" /></Form>` with a value the schema rejects.
claims.wrongResult: The control renders no `aria-invalid` and no `data-invalid`, so the error state reaches neither assistive tech nor the recipe's invalid ring — a bound RangeSlider looks valid while its field holds errors, where the single-thumb Slider beside it rings.
claims.contract: TSDoc on `FormValueResult.invalid` (`use-form-value.ts`): "Pass to `useControlProps`; the field's error state merges into `invalid`."
claims.evidence: range-slider.tsx:74-82 — `useFormValue` returns `invalid`, but the destructure takes only `{ value, setValue }`; the root div (lines 124-135) and both thumbs (lines 151-184) carry no validation attributes and the file never imports `useControlProps` or `invalidAttrs`. Compare slider.tsx:69, :88-93 and :111 (`{...invalidAttrs(controlProps.invalid)}`). Suspected severity: low-moderate (silent validation state). Fix: destructure `invalid`, feed it through `useControlProps`, and spread the resulting `validation` on the root.

claims.trigger: Render `<ColorPicker />` and open it.
claims.wrongResult: Floating UI stamps `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` onto the picker's positioning wrapper `<div data-slot="control">`, which carries no widget role. Two nested elements then report the same expanded state (the wrapper and the trigger button), and the generic div carries popup attributes its role does not allow — an `aria-allowed-attr` failure.
claims.contract: TSDoc on `useFloatingUI`'s `role` option: "Pass `null` when the component hand-rolls its own roles on inner elements (the trigger button and the panel); a role here also stamps the positioning wrapper, nesting a duplicate widget around the real one (combobox-in-combobox, listbox-in-listbox)."
claims.evidence: use-color-picker-state.ts:73-80 passes `role: 'dialog'` to `useFloatingUI`; use-floating-ui.ts:433 enables `useRole` whenever `roleProp !== null`, which emits the reference props. color-picker-trigger.tsx:63 spreads `{...getReferenceProps()}` on the bare wrapper div, while lines 71-76 already hand-roll `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded={open}` on the Button, and color-picker-content.tsx:58-59 already hand-rolls `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal` on the panel. combobox.tsx:552-554 is the in-repo precedent: `role: null` with the comment "The input and panel carry their own roles + popup wiring; `role: null` suppresses floating-ui's wrapper roles." Suspected severity: moderate (a11y). Fix: pass `role: null` in use-color-picker-state.ts:78.

claims.trigger: `<ColorPanel value="#ff0000" onValueChange={() => {}} />` (a controlled panel whose owner does not adopt the reported value) — then drag the hue slider or the saturation area.
claims.wrongResult: The panel paints and keeps reporting the dragged colour while the `value` prop still says `#ff0000`. The control drifts permanently away from its controlled prop and never snaps back, so the rendered colour no longer reflects the value the consumer holds.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §7.2: "Resolution order on every control: an explicit `value`/`checked` prop wins, then the bound field, then internal (uncontrolled) state." The hook's own TSDoc: "Owns the HSVA and reconciles against the `value` prop, skipping echoes of its own emission, compared on the serialised form."
claims.evidence: use-color-state.ts:62-75 — the reconcile effect is keyed on `[value]` alone, and lines 84-88 in `setHsva` write the newly emitted value into `cacheRef` and into `setInternal`. When the consumer does not echo the emission back, `value` never changes, the effect never re-runs, and the internal state stays ahead of the prop; the echo guard at line 66 would also suppress a later reconcile against the unchanged prop. Suspected severity: moderate (broken controlled contract; a consumer cannot veto or normalise a colour). Fix: reconcile against the serialised current state rather than only on `value` identity — e.g. compare `serializeColor(hsva, format, alpha)` with `value` each commit, or add the internal value to the effect's deps.

claims.trigger: `<Field><Label>Resume</Label><FileUpload variant="input" /></Field>`
claims.wrongResult: The presentational readonly `<Input>` adopts the field's generated id from Control context, so the `<Label>` names the display box instead of the real `<input type="file">`, which is left named only by the `'Choose a file'` placeholder. The visible input also inherits the field's `required`, so a decorative control announces itself as the required one.
claims.contract: TSDoc `@remarks` on `FileUpload`: "The visually-hidden input is the real control in every variant and carries the accessible name; the visible trigger is presentational."
claims.evidence: file-upload.tsx:166-176 renders `<Input readOnly size={size} disabled={disabled} value={label ?? ''} …>` with no `id` and no `required={false}`; input.tsx:73-83 resolves them through `useControlProps`, and use-control-props.ts:89/:92 return `input.id ?? control?.id` and `input.required ?? control?.required`. The hidden input at file-upload.tsx:154-163 gets only `ariaLabel={placeholder ?? 'Choose a file'}`. The in-repo counter-example is color-hex-input.tsx:17/:41 and color-channel-inputs.tsx:21/:68, which pin an explicit scoped `id` on inner Inputs for exactly this reason. Suspected severity: moderate (WCAG 1.3.1/4.1.2 — the field label does not name the control). Fix: pass an explicit scoped `id` and `required={false}` to the display Input, and thread the Control label id onto the hidden file input.

claims.trigger: `<Field required severity="error"><Label>Brand colour</Label><Message>Pick a colour</Message><ColorPanel /></Field>`
claims.wrongResult: Each R/G/B(/A) number input inherits the enclosing field's `required` and `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader repeats the field's description and error text on every channel input, and four sub-part inputs each announce themselves as the required control of the field.
claims.contract: TSDoc on `ColorChannelInputs`: "Per-channel RGB(A) numeric entry, two-way bound to the panel's colour." They are panel sub-parts bound to `ColorPanelContext`, not the enclosing field's control.
claims.evidence: color-channel-inputs.tsx:66-84 passes `id`, `disabled`, `size`, `type`, `min`, `max` and `aria-label` to `<Input>` but neither `required={false}` nor an `aria-describedby`; input.tsx:73-81 hands those to `useControlProps`, which at use-control-props.ts:73 and :92 merges `control?.describedBy` and falls back to `control?.required`. The same shape repeats at color-hex-input.tsx:39-55. The panel's own `disabled` is passed explicitly (line 77), which shows the intended pattern for shielding these sub-parts. Suspected severity: low (verbose/duplicated announcements). Fix: pass `required={false}` and an empty/pinned `aria-describedby` on the channel and hex inputs, or wrap the panel body in a Control reset.

claims.trigger: `<Combobox multiple clearOnEmpty value={picked} onValueChange={setPicked} displayValue={fmt}>…</Combobox>` — pick two options, then select the input text and delete it.
claims.wrongResult: The selection is not cleared. `clearOnEmpty` is silently a no-op under `multiple`: the query empties, editing ends on the next commit, and the field paints the "2 selected" summary again over a selection the user just tried to empty.
claims.contract: TSDoc on `ComboboxBaseProps.clearOnEmpty`: "Clears the value when the user empties the input while editing." No `multiple` carve-out is stated.
claims.evidence: use-combobox-input.ts:118-120 — `if (clearOnEmpty && next === '' && !multiple && value !== undefined) { setValue(undefined) }`. The `!multiple` term is undocumented; the prop doc (combobox.tsx:118-119) states the behaviour unconditionally. Suspected severity: low (a documented prop does nothing in one mode). Fix: clear to `[] as T[]` under `multiple`, or state the carve-out in the prop's TSDoc.

claims.trigger: `<RadioGroup role="group" aria-label="Plan">…</RadioGroup>` (or any wrapper that forwards a `role` through the rest props).
claims.wrongResult: The consumer's `role` overwrites the hard-coded `radiogroup`, so the container renders as a plain group and assistive tech no longer announces the set as a radio group or reports "1 of 3" positions.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state, and the resolved wiring of the §7.2 binding cascade — are written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't drop a row out of roving…" The component's own TSDoc: "Group layout container for a set of {@link Radio} controls, rendered as a `role="radiogroup"`."
claims.evidence: radio-group.tsx:25 — `return <ToggleGroup role="radiogroup" {...props} />`; `role` is written before the spread and `RadioGroupProps` (lines 11-12) omits only `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` from the div attributes, so `role` stays typeable and wins. `ToggleGroup` itself destructures `role` (toggle.tsx:12-13), so the consumer value reaches the DOM. Suspected severity: low. Fix: write `role="radiogroup"` after `{...props}`, or omit `role` from `RadioGroupProps`.

claims.trigger: `<CheckboxGroup role="presentation" aria-labelledby="plan-label">…</CheckboxGroup>`
claims.wrongResult: The consumer's `role` overwrites the hard-coded `group`, so the container loses the grouping semantics the component documents and the shared `aria-labelledby` label no longer names a group for assistive tech.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state … are written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't drop a row out of roving…" The component's own TSDoc: "Stacks related CheckboxFields under a shared group layout, exposing them as a `role="group"` to assistive tech."
claims.evidence: checkbox-group.tsx:12 — `return <ToggleGroup role="group" {...props} />`; `CheckboxGroupProps = ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'>` (line 5) keeps `role` typeable, and `ToggleGroup` destructures `role` (toggle.tsx:12-13) so the consumer value reaches the DOM. Same shape as radio-group.tsx:25. Suspected severity: low. Fix: write `role="group"` after `{...props}`, or omit `role` from `CheckboxGroupProps`.

leads.note: `toggle` resolves multi-select membership with `arr.includes(newValue)` and `arr.filter((v) => v !== newValue)` (lines 50-52), i.e. reference identity. A Combobox/Listbox over object options whose parent re-creates the option objects between renders can never deselect a picked item — the second click appends a second entry instead of removing the first. The hook's TSDoc says only "toggling adds / removes entries" and states no identity requirement.

`{...rest}` is spread last (line 112), after `type`, `id`, `name`, `value={valueState.value}`, `onChange`, `onBlur` and `{...validation}` — the inverse of the §3.9 order that `switch.tsx` sets. `InputProps` omits `value` but not `defaultValue`, so `<Form defaultValues={{a:'x'}}><Input name="a" defaultValue="y" /></Form>` puts `defaultValue` on the same element as the bound `value` (React controlled/uncontrolled error), and the bound field does not ignore `defaultValue` as CONVENTIONS §7.2 requires.

claims.trigger: Render the fallback (non-element-child) form inside a form element with a colliding structural prop, e.g. `<MenuTrigger type="submit">Actions</MenuTrigger>` or `<MenuTrigger aria-expanded={false}>`.
claims.wrongResult: The consumer prop wins over the trigger's own wiring: the button becomes a form-submit control that posts the enclosing form on every open click, and `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`/`data-slot` are equally clobberable, so assistive tech reads a stale disclosure state and the `data-slot` test anchor disappears.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state, and the resolved wiring of the §7.2 binding cascade — are written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't drop a row out of roving, turn a button into a form submit, or clobber a bound field; `menu-item.tsx` is the composite precedent".
claims.evidence: menu-trigger.tsx lines 140-160: the `<button>` writes `type="button"`, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `data-slot` on lines 143-147 and then spreads `{...getReferenceProps({...rest})}` on line 149, where `rest` is the consumer's own `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'>` (destructured at lines 134-138). floating-ui's `getReferenceProps` passes unknown user props straight through, so they land last and win. The cloned-child branch (lines 113-131) does it correctly — `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`/`data-slot` sit after the spread — so the two branches disagree. Compare `menu-item.tsx` lines 129-152, the section's named precedent. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: hoist the structural attributes below the `getReferenceProps` spread in the fallback branch, mirroring the clone branch.

claims.trigger: Open a right-click `ContextMenu` (or a `defaultOpen` static `Menu`), arrow to a link row `<MenuItem href="/settings" onAction={fn}>Settings</MenuItem>`, and press Space.
claims.wrongResult: Nothing happens: `onAction` never fires, the menu stays open, and the page behind the panel scrolls instead. The identical row activates on Space in a dropdown menu, so the same component answers Space in one mode and ignores it in another.
claims.contract: MenuItem TSDoc: "Renders an anchor when `href` is set (keeping middle-click and open-in-new-tab working), a `<button>` otherwise. … Fires `onAction` and closes the menu on click or Enter/Space."
claims.evidence: menu-item.tsx: the `<button>` branch composes `onKeyDown={... handleMenuItemKeyDown(event, consumerOnKeyDown, handleSelect, disabled)}` at lines 149-151, but the `href` branch (lines 95-114) wires only `onClick` and `onPointerMove` — no `handleMenuItemKeyDown`. Anchors fire a native click on Enter but never on Space. The panel-level roving that would cover it (`popover.tsx` `PopoverPanel` lines 96-101) runs `useA11yRoving` in the default `mode: 'focus'`, and `handleActivationKey` in `hooks/a11y/use-a11y-roving.ts` line 595 returns early unless `ctx.isVirtual`, so no activation key reaches a focus-roved anchor. Only the dropdown path works, via `use-menu-state.ts` line 143 `activationKey: MENU_ACTIVATION_KEYS`. Suspected severity: medium (APG menu pattern requires Space). Fix: add the same composed `onKeyDown={handleMenuItemKeyDown(...)}` after the spread in the link branch.

claims.trigger: Render a right-click context menu — `<Menu>` with no `placement` and no `defaultOpen` — whose panel is `<MenuContent aria-label="Row actions">…</MenuContent>`.
claims.wrongResult: The `aria-label` is silently discarded; the rendered `role="menu"` panel ships with no accessible name at all, and neither does `aria-labelledby`. A right-click menu has no trigger to borrow a name from, so the surface is an unnamed menu for assistive tech.
claims.contract: MenuContentProps TSDoc: "Props for {@link MenuContent}: an optional accessible name for `static` menus" with `'aria-label'?: string` declared on the public prop type; MenuContent TSDoc: "The menu panel: a `role=\"menu\"` surface with roving focus and typeahead over its items."
claims.evidence: menu-content.tsx: `ariaLabel`/`ariaLabelledby` are destructured at lines 36-37 and forwarded to `PopoverPanel` only in the `isStatic` branch (lines 65-66). The floating branch (lines 82-119) passes `id`, `role`, `autoFocus`, `trapTab`, `typeahead`, `glass`, `className`, `onKeyDown` but never the two label props, so they are dropped for both dropdown and right-click modes. `use-menu-state.ts` line 98 shows the third mode, `isContextMenu = !isDropdown && !isStatic`, which by construction has no trigger. `PopoverPanel` already accepts both props (popover.tsx lines 37-38, 129-130). Suspected severity: medium (a11y). Fix: forward `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` in the floating branch too, or gate them on `!isDropdown` so a dropdown keeps its trigger-derived name.

claims.trigger: `<TabList aria-label="Sections" onKeyDown={(e) => logShortcut(e)}>…</TabList>` — a consumer attaching any keydown listener to the tab list.
claims.wrongResult: Arrow-key roving stops entirely: Left/Right (or Up/Down under vertical orientation) no longer move focus between tabs, because the consumer handler replaces the roving handler rather than composing with it. The list keeps `role="tablist"` and its single Tab stop, so keyboard users get trapped on one tab.
claims.contract: TabList TSDoc: "`role=\"tablist\"` container for `<Tab>` children. Manages roving focus along the resolved `orientation`"; CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: load-bearing structural attributes and "the resolved wiring" are "written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't drop a row out of roving".
claims.evidence: tab-list.tsx lines 82-95: the div writes `role="tablist"`, `aria-orientation`, and `onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}` (line 89) and then spreads `{...props}` (line 91). `TabListProps` (lines 15-16) is `AccessibleName & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'>, 'aria-label' | 'aria-labelledby'>`, so `onKeyDown` and `role` are both in the consumer surface. The sibling navigation roots do this correctly: `sidebar.tsx` lines 78-81 compose `handleKeyDown(event); onKeyDown?.(event)`. Suspected severity: high (keyboard navigation loss). Fix: destructure `onKeyDown` and compose it with `handleKeyDown`, and move `role`/`aria-orientation` below the spread.

claims.trigger: `<StepperStep value={1}><StepperIndicator>2</StepperIndicator><StepperTitle>Details</StepperTitle></StepperStep>` — any indicator given children (a step number or a checkmark icon).
claims.wrongResult: The children never render. The marker shows only the bare recipe dot, so a numbered or checkmarked stepper silently loses every glyph the caller supplied, with no type error to warn them.
claims.contract: StepperIndicator TSDoc: "The leading marker of a {@link StepperStep} (number, checkmark, or dot) styled by the step's state." — and `StepperIndicatorProps` is `{ className?: string } & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'span'>, 'className'>`, which includes `children`.
claims.evidence: stepper-indicator.tsx lines 39-50: `children` is never destructured, so it stays inside `...props` and is spread onto the `<span>` at line 43 — but the element also has explicit JSX children on lines 45-48 (the `ActiveIndicator` and the sr-only state text). JSX compiles explicit children into the `children` key after the spread, so `props.children` is overwritten and dropped. Every sibling slot in the family renders self-closing and therefore does forward children: `stepper-title.tsx` lines 18-22, `stepper-separator.tsx` lines 22-28. The recipe confirms no glyph comes from CSS — `recipes/kata/stepper.ts` lines 68-74 give `indicator.base` only `size-3.5`, `rounded.full`, and a background colour. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: destructure `children` and render it inside the span before the sr-only suffix.

claims.trigger: `<SidebarItem suffix={<Badge>3</Badge>}><SidebarLabel>Inbox</SidebarLabel><SidebarItemActions><IconButton …/></SidebarItemActions></SidebarItem>` — an explicit `suffix` prop together with a `SidebarItemActions` child.
claims.wrongResult: The `SidebarItemActions` subtree vanishes from the DOM entirely. It is filtered out of the inner content because an actions child was found, but the explicit `suffix` wins the slot, so the actions button is rendered nowhere and its controls become unreachable by pointer and keyboard.
claims.contract: SidebarItemActions TSDoc: "Hoisted into the item's `suffix` slot, so its contents render beside the row's button … Equivalent to passing the same content to the `suffix` prop; an explicit `suffix` wins." and SidebarItem TSDoc: "a `SidebarItemActions` child hoists into the `suffix` slot (an explicit `suffix` prop wins)".
claims.evidence: sidebar-item.tsx lines 36-48: `actions` is found on line 39; `inner` is computed on line 43 as `actions ? childArray.filter((child) => child !== actions) : children` — the filter is gated only on an actions child existing, not on whether the hoist actually happened; line 47 returns `suffix: suffix ?? actions`, so with an explicit `suffix` the actions node is neither the suffix nor part of `inner`. Content loss, not merely a slot override. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: filter the actions child out of `inner` only when it wins the suffix slot — `const hoisted = suffix === undefined ? actions : undefined` and key both the filter and the returned suffix off `hoisted`.

claims.trigger: `<NavItem value="reports" aria-current="location">Reports</NavItem>` — or any NavItem given `type` (e.g. `type="submit"` inside a form).
claims.wrongResult: The consumer prop overrides NavItem's own wiring: the resolved `aria-current="page"` marker is replaced (so the current link is no longer announced as the current page while the visual active indicator still shows), and `type="button"` can be turned into a form submit so clicking a nav link posts the enclosing form.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state, and the resolved wiring of the §7.2 binding cascade — are written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't drop a row out of roving, turn a button into a form submit, or clobber a bound field".
claims.evidence: nav-item.tsx lines 69-77: `<Button type="button" data-slot="nav-item-inner" data-current={dataAttr(item.current)} aria-current={item.current ? 'page' : undefined} className={…} onClick={item.handleClick} {...props} />` — `{...props}` is last (line 76). `NavMenuItemProps` extends `PolymorphicProps<'button', 'color' | 'ref' | 'prefix'>` (use-nav-item.ts line 42), so `type`, `aria-current`, `data-slot` and `role` are all in the consumer surface. `Button` itself destructures `type` and renders it (button.tsx lines 94, 178), so the override reaches the DOM. Suspected severity: low-to-medium. Fix: move `type`, `data-slot`, `data-current`, and `aria-current` below the `{...props}` spread, as `menu-item.tsx` lines 136-142 do.

claims.trigger: `<SidebarList><SidebarItem current aria-current="true"><SidebarLabel>Home</SidebarLabel></SidebarItem>…</SidebarList>` — a SidebarItem given its own `aria-current` value.
claims.wrongResult: The consumer value replaces the resolved `aria-current="page"`, so the Sidebar's roving resting stop no longer matches its `[aria-current="page"]` selector and the single Tab stop silently falls back to the first item instead of the current page. `type` and `data-slot` are overridable the same way; overriding `data-slot` also drops the row out of the roving item set entirely.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: load-bearing structural attributes and "widget ARIA state … are written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't drop a row out of roving"; Sidebar TSDoc: "the resting stop sits on the current page (`aria-current=\"page\"`), falling back to the first item".
claims.evidence: sidebar-item.tsx lines 101-115: `<Button type="button" data-slot="sidebar-item-inner" data-current={…} aria-current={item.current ? 'page' : undefined} className={…} onClick={item.handleClick} {...props}>` — spread last on line 114. The roving config that depends on both attributes is in sidebar.tsx lines 45-60: `itemSelector: '[data-slot="sidebar-item-inner"]:not(:disabled)'` and `activeSelector: '[aria-current="page"]'`, resolved by `resolveRestingStop` in hooks/a11y/use-a11y-roving.ts lines 336-351. `SidebarItemProps` is `NavItemProps & { size }`, and `NavItemProps` carries the full `PolymorphicProps<'button', …>` surface. Suspected severity: low-to-medium. Fix: write `type`, `data-slot`, `data-current`, and `aria-current` after the spread.

claims.trigger: `<Tabs defaultValue="a"><TabList …/><TabContents><TabContent value="a" id="overview-panel">…</TabContent></TabContents></Tabs>` — a panel given its own `id` (a scroll anchor or deep-link target).
claims.wrongResult: The consumer `id` replaces the derived panel id, so the matching `<Tab>`'s `aria-controls` points at an element that no longer exists — a dangling ARIA reference — while the panel's `aria-labelledby` still names the tab. `role="tabpanel"` and the computed `tabIndex` are overridable the same way.
claims.contract: TabContent TSDoc: "Inside `<Tabs>` it auto-wires `role=\"tabpanel\"`, `aria-labelledby` to the matching tab, and a computed `tabIndex` (`0` when the panel has no focusable child, per APG), pairing with its `Tab` via the Tabs base id + value"; CONVENTIONS.md §3.9 on writing "the resolved wiring" after `{...props}`.
claims.evidence: tab-contents.tsx lines 80-93: the auto-wiring object `{...(auto && { role: 'tabpanel', id: panelId, 'aria-labelledby': triggerId, tabIndex })}` is written on lines 86-91 and `{...props}` follows on line 92. `CurrentContentProps` extends `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'>`, so `id`, `role`, and `tabIndex` are all in the surface. The counterpart id lives in tab.tsx lines 124-134 / 188-190 (`aria-controls={… controlsId}`), derived from the same `useA11yDisclosure({ id: baseId, key: value })`. Note `Tab` itself gets the order right (tab.tsx line 178 spreads `{...rest}` first, then the wiring). Suspected severity: low-to-medium. Fix: spread `{...props}` before the auto-wiring block.

claims.trigger: `<StepperPanels><StepperPanel value={0} id="details">…</StepperPanel></StepperPanels>` — a panel given its own `id` or `aria-labelledby`.
claims.wrongResult: The disclosure wiring is clobbered: the `<StepperStep>`'s `aria-controls` still points at the derived panel id, which now names nothing, so the step→panel reference dangles and the panel loses its `aria-labelledby` link back to the step button.
claims.contract: StepperPanel TSDoc: "Emits a `<section>` whose disclosure ids match the corresponding {@link StepperStep} for `aria-controls` wiring"; CONVENTIONS.md §3.9 requires "the resolved wiring" to be "written *after* `{...props}`".
claims.evidence: stepper-panel.tsx line 41: `<section {...panelProps} data-slot="stepper-panel" className={className} {...props}>` — `panelProps` (`{ id: panelId, 'aria-labelledby': triggerId }`, built in hooks/a11y/use-a11y-disclosure.ts lines 83-86) is written first and `{...props}` last. `StepperPanelProps` is `{ value: number; className?: string } & Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'div'>, 'className'>`, so `id` and `aria-labelledby` are exposed. The matching consumer is stepper-step.tsx lines 136-138 (`aria-controls={… panelId : undefined}`). Suspected severity: low-to-medium. Fix: reorder to `<section {...props} {...panelProps} data-slot=… className={className}>`.

claims.trigger: Render a `<Toolbar aria-label="Editor">` whose controls interleave element kinds in DOM order — an `<a href>` between two `<button>`s, say — then press ArrowRight from the first control under the jsdom test suite.
claims.wrongResult: Arrow navigation visits the controls grouped by selector rather than in DOM order, so the second press lands on the trailing anchor instead of the adjacent button, and the roving resting `tabIndex=0` is seated on the wrong control.
claims.contract: Toolbar TSDoc: "ARIA toolbar grouping related controls with roving-tabindex arrow-key navigation along its `orientation`"; the repository's own recorded caveat in hooks/a11y/use-a11y-roving.ts `rowControls`: "Spec orders selector-list matches by document position, but jsdom (nwsapi) groups them by selector; sort so arrow order is the DOM order."
claims.evidence: toolbar-constants.ts lines 1-12 join seven selectors (`a[href]`, `button:not(:disabled)`, `[tabindex="0"]`, `[tabindex="-1"]`, three role selectors) into one list; toolbar.tsx lines 38-43 hands it to `useA11yRoving` as `itemSelector`. That path resolves items through `queryItems` (use-a11y-roving.ts lines 61-65), which returns `Array.from(container.querySelectorAll(selector))` with no document-position sort — unlike `rowControls` (lines 46-58), which sorts precisely because of the nwsapi behaviour the codebase documents. Every other roving consumer in this scope passes a single selector (`MENUITEM_SELECTOR`, `TAB_SELECTOR`, the sidebar and command-palette item selectors), so Toolbar is the only exposed caller. Suspected severity: low (browser-correct, jsdom-suite observable). Fix: sort inside `queryItems`, or sort in `Toolbar` before use.

claims.trigger: A host builds its `defaults` with the public `mergeContextMenuItems([groupA, groupB])` and feeds the result into `resolveContextMenuEntries(config, defaults)` while the caller's `config.items` is non-empty.
claims.wrongResult: Two entries carry the same React key `context-menu-group-1`: the separator minted by the inner merge and the one minted by the outer merge. React logs a duplicate-key warning and can reuse the wrong row's state across a re-render, so a menu re-order shows a separator where an item belongs.
claims.contract: mergeContextMenuItems TSDoc: "Joins non-empty groups of entries with a separator between each … The building block a host uses to set its own default groups apart"; ContextMenuSeparator TSDoc: "Stable identity for the separator, used as its React key."
claims.evidence: context-menu-merge.ts lines 12-18 mint `key: \`context-menu-group-${index}\`` from the index within `kept`, and lines 43-45 call `mergeContextMenuItems` again over the already-merged `defaults`, so both passes emit index 1. Both functions are public — context-menu/index.ts line 3 re-exports them — so the composition is reachable through the documented surface, despite the in-file comment on lines 40-42 calling it "Latent, unreachable today". `ContextMenuList` consumes the key directly at context-menu-list.tsx line 27. Suspected severity: low. Fix: derive the separator key from a caller-supplied prefix, or from the surviving group's first entry key, so nested merges cannot collide.

claims.trigger: A controlled stepper whose owner clears the value: `<Stepper value={step} onValueChange={setStep}>` where `step` transitions from `2` to `undefined` (the `null` alternative is rejected at the type level, since `value?: number`).
claims.wrongResult: The stepper silently flips from controlled to uncontrolled and jumps to the shadow internal value (step 0), and subsequent step clicks mutate that shadow state without the owner's `value` ever agreeing. There is no way to keep a Stepper controlled with no current step, unlike its sibling roots.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §7.3: "In value props, `undefined` leaves the control uncontrolled; `null` keeps it controlled with no current value."
claims.evidence: stepper.tsx lines 16-22 declare `value?: number` / `defaultValue?: number` with no `null` arm, and lines 95-99 call `useControllable<number>({ value, defaultValue: defaultValue ?? 0, … })`. `hooks/use-controllable.ts` lines 32-34 decide controlled-ness with `value !== undefined`, and its own TSDoc (lines 9-10) states the §7.3 contract: "`undefined` leaves the hook uncontrolled; pass `null` to stay controlled with no current value." The sibling current-item roots in this scope both expose the null arm — tabs.tsx line 12 `value?: string | null`, nav.tsx line 10 `value?: string | null` — so Stepper is the outlier. Suspected severity: low. Fix: widen to `value?: number | null` and pass it straight through to `useControllable`, matching Tabs and Nav.

claims.trigger: `<CommandPaletteItem href="/admin" disabled>Admin</CommandPaletteItem>`, then middle-click the row (or right-click it and choose "Open in new tab").
claims.wrongResult: The disabled entry navigates: a new tab opens on `/admin`. Only the left-click path is guarded, so a row that renders dimmed and `aria-disabled` still acts on the auxiliary pointer paths.
claims.contract: CommandPaletteItem TSDoc: "`disabled` items are inert on every input path", restated in the handler comment: "the disabled guard runs before the consumer handler: disabled items are inert on every input path, and preventDefault keeps disabled link items from navigating."
claims.evidence: command-palette-item.tsx lines 52-68: `handleSelect` calls `event.preventDefault()` for a disabled item, but it is wired only as `onClick` (line 81) on a `LinkComponent` that still carries a live `href` (lines 84-89, `forwardedProps` retains `href`). Middle-click fires `auxclick`, not `click`, and the browser's own "Open in new tab" fires neither, so both bypass the guard. The sibling row in the same scope handles exactly this: menu-item.tsx lines 64-82 renders a disabled link as an inert `<span>` with no `href`, with the comment "Anchors with `href` are navigable via middle-click, Cmd-click, and 'Open in new tab', none of which fire `onClick`." Suspected severity: medium. Fix: mirror MenuItem — render the disabled link arm as a `role="option"` `<span>` carrying no `href`.

claims.trigger: A consumer writes against the exported pair, e.g. `const nav: NavContextValue = useNavContext()` or `useNavContext().value` in an app component.
claims.wrongResult: `turbo run check-types` fails: the hook's real return type is `CurrentContextValue | undefined`, which is not assignable to the exported `NavContextValue`, and a direct property read on the result is a possibly-undefined access. The documented contract and the actual signature disagree, so the public type is unusable as written.
claims.contract: nav/context.ts TSDoc: "Value broadcast by {@link NavContext}: the active `value` and its change callback" for `export type NavContextValue = CurrentContextValue`, and "Reads the enclosing {@link Nav} selection state ({@link NavContextValue})." for `useNavContext`.
claims.evidence: nav/context.ts lines 7-15: `NavContextValue = CurrentContextValue` (no `| undefined`), `NavContext = CurrentContext`, and `useNavContext()` just returns `useCurrent()`. But `primitives/current/current.ts` lines 24-27 create the context as `createContext<CurrentContextValue | undefined>('Current', { default: undefined })`, so `useCurrent()` — and therefore `useNavContext()` — returns `CurrentContextValue | undefined`. Both symbols are on the public surface via nav/index.ts line 2. Suspected severity: low. Fix: declare `export type NavContextValue = CurrentContextValue | undefined`, or give `useNavContext` an explicit `: NavContextValue | undefined` return annotation and say so in the TSDoc.

leads.note: `queryItems` (lines 61-65) returns `Array.from(container.querySelectorAll(selector))` with no document-position sort, while `rowControls` in the same file (lines 46-58) sorts precisely because "jsdom (nwsapi) groups them by selector". Any `useA11yRoving` caller that passes a multi-selector `itemSelector` therefore roves out of DOM order under jsdom. Also: `handleActivationKey` (line 595) bails unless `ctx.isVirtual`, so `activationKey` is silently inert for every focus-mode roving surface.

`PopoverPanel`'s autofocus `useLayoutEffect` (lines 105-117) depends on `[autoFocus, itemSelector, scrollWithin]` but not on the rendered rows, so a panel whose options mount a commit later (a virtualized or async list) never seats focus on the selected row and drops it on the panel container instead. The panel also hardcodes `mode: 'focus'` roving, which makes the `activationKey` contract unreachable for every menu that roves by real focus.

The `render` arm calls `cloneElement(render, linkProps, children)` (line 70) where `linkProps` always contains `className` (line 65). cloneElement merges the config over the element's own props, so a call site writing `render={<Link className="…" />}` has its className silently replaced by the host's rather than merged, unlike every other className path in the library, which goes through `cn`.

claims.trigger: Render a read-only board (`<Kanban columns={…} getKey={…}>` with `onReorder` omitted, or `disabled`) and give a card an explicit accessible name: `<KanbanCard cardId="t-1" aria-label="Task 1: deploy">`.
claims.wrongResult: The `aria-label` is never written to the DOM. The card falls back to its content-derived name, so the override the caller asked for is silently discarded on every non-interactive board.
claims.contract: KanbanCardProps['aria-label'] TSDoc: "Overrides the card's accessible name. By default the card is named by its own content; dnd-kit already announces draggability (`aria-roledescription`) and keyboard instructions (`aria-describedby`). Only set this when the content doesn't yield a usable name." Nothing in the contract scopes the override to interactive boards.
claims.evidence: kanban-card.tsx line 75: `aria-label={interactive ? ariaLabel : undefined}`. `interactive` comes from `useKanbanContext()` (line 37), set in kanban.tsx line 58 as `!disabled && !!onReorder`. The neighbouring gates on lines 69-74 (ref, style, attributes, listeners, onKeyDown, onBlur) are all drag wiring and correctly gated; `aria-label` is a naming concern, not drag wiring, and got swept into the same ternary. Contrast KanbanColumn, which passes `aria-label={ariaLabel}` unconditionally (kanban-column.tsx line 70). Suspected severity: low-medium (a11y regression, silent). Fix: write `aria-label={ariaLabel}` unconditionally.

claims.trigger:
Render the body with two conditional card slots that both evaluate false: `No cards

}>{showA && }{showB && }`.
claims.wrongResult: `children` is the array `[false, false]`, so the length check reports children present. The body renders nothing at all and the `empty` placeholder is suppressed, leaving a blank column with no empty-state message.
claims.contract: KanbanColumnBodyProps.empty TSDoc: "Shown when the column has no cards." and the component TSDoc: "Scrollable card region of a {@link KanbanColumn}; renders its cards, or the `empty` placeholder when there are none."
claims.evidence: kanban-column-body.tsx line 15: `const hasChildren = Array.isArray(children) ? children.length > 0 : children != null`. The array branch counts slots, not renderable nodes, so `false`/`null`/`undefined` entries count as cards. The non-array branch has the mirror hole: a single `{showA && <KanbanCard/>}` child yields `false`, and `false != null` is true, so the placeholder is suppressed there too. Suspected severity: medium (empty state disappears on a routine conditional-render pattern). Fix: use `Children.toArray(children).length > 0`, which drops null/undefined/false and flattens arrays — the same helper tree-item.tsx line 69 already uses for exactly this reason.

claims.trigger: On an interactive board, drag a card from column A and drop it directly on a card Y that sits in column B, releasing the pointer without moving again after the insertion preview appears.
claims.wrongResult: `onReorder` fires twice for one drop and the card lands one slot below where the live preview showed it — after Y instead of before Y.
claims.contract: The handler's own stated contract, use-kanban-drag.ts: "Cross-column moves apply in dragOver; skip them here." and the hook TSDoc: "applies cross-column moves live on drag-over and commits same-column reorders on drag-end".
claims.evidence: applyKanbanDragOver (lines 23-81) already spliced the card into `overCol` at `insertIdx = overCardIdx` and called `onReorder(next)`. By the time handleDragEnd runs (lines 140-176) the `columns` prop reflects that move, so `findColumnByCardId(activeCardId)` (line 155) now returns column B and the cross-column guard `if (activeCol.id !== overCol.id) return` (line 162) can never fire for a cross-column drop. Lines 164-170 then compute oldIdx = k (the card, freshly inserted before Y) and newIdx = k+1 (Y) and run `arrayMove`, swapping them. The guard tests post-move state to detect a pre-move condition. Suspected severity: medium; timing-dependent — a further pointer move usually retargets `over` onto the dragged card itself, which short-circuits both handlers on line 39/153. Fix: capture the origin column id in a ref at handleDragStart and skip dragEnd when it differs from the card's current column.

claims.trigger: In a reorderable list (`<List items={…} getKey={…} onReorder={fn}>`), render a row that links but is a target in name only: `<ListItem href="/docs/1" interactive={false}><ListLabel>Doc</ListLabel></ListItem>`.
claims.wrongResult: The row grows two Tab stops: the `<li>` takes `tabIndex=0` for the reorder gestures while the rendered `<a href>` stays natively tabbable. A keyboard user tabs twice per row, and the two stops are visually indistinguishable.
claims.contract: ListItem TSDoc @remarks: "A reorderable row has exactly ONE Tab stop.
