An interactive content area is natively focusable, so the reorder keys ride it and the `<li>` takes no focus … A display-only row has nothing focusable inside, so there the `<li>` is the stop. Wiring both put two indistinguishable stops on every row: one to move it, one to activate it."
claims.evidence: list-item.tsx lines 150-151: `const stopOnContent = reorderable && interactive` / `const stopOnRow = reorderable && !interactive`, where `interactive = interactiveProp ?? activates` (line 127) and `activates = href !== undefined || props.onClick !== undefined` (line 122). The stop placement keys off `interactive` (a styling/treatment flag the caller may override) instead of `activates` (whether the content area is natively focusable). With `interactive={false}` and `href` set, stopOnRow is true so reorderProps lands on the `<li>` (line 187) with `tabIndex: tabIndex ?? 0` (line 165), while Polymorphic renders a real anchor (primitives/polymorphic/polymorphic.tsx lines 48-59). The mirror case also breaks: `interactive` forced true on "a row whose only handler sits on a child" — the documented second use case on lines 30-34 — puts tabIndex 0 on a plain content div while the child control stays focusable. Suspected severity: medium (a11y; the invariant the TSDoc calls out by name). Fix: derive the stops from `activates`, not `interactive` — `stopOnContent = reorderable && activates`, `stopOnRow = reorderable && !activates`.

claims.trigger: Render a read-only list of duplicate primitives with no key extractor: `<List items={['draft', 'draft', 'sent']} sortable={false}>{(s) => <ListItem><ListLabel>{s}</ListLabel></ListItem>}</List>`.
claims.wrongResult: Both `'draft'` entries resolve to the same key, so React logs a duplicate-key warning, the two rows share one `data-item-id`, and the keyboard/DOM lookups that resolve a row by that id can only ever reach the second one.
claims.contract: ListProps.getKey TSDoc on the read-only arm: "Stable key extractor. Optional when the list is read-only; falls back to item index." and useListDrag TSDoc: "derives a stable key extractor (falling back to item index for read-only lists)".
claims.evidence: use-list-drag.ts lines 25-27: `const indexByItem = new Map(items.map((item, index) => [item, index] as const))` then `(item) => String(indexByItem.get(item) ?? -1)`. The Map is keyed by item value, so equal primitives overwrite each other and every duplicate resolves to the LAST index — `new Map([['draft',0],['draft',1]])` yields only `'draft' -> 1`. It is a value-to-index lookup, not the promised positional index. Consumed at list.tsx line 146 (`const id = effectiveGetKey(item)`) as both the React key and the `data-item-id` written on the `<li>` (list-item.tsx line 189), which use-list-keyboard.ts line 122 queries via `querySlot`. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: pass the render index into the fallback, or key the Map only when items are objects and fall back to the positional index otherwise.

claims.trigger: Render `<Listbox disabled value={v} onValueChange={fn}><ListboxOption value="a">A</ListboxOption></Listbox>` and click the chevron, the prefix slot, or the frame padding beside the trigger button.
claims.wrongResult: The menu opens on a disabled control and the focus manager moves focus into the portalled panel, where options are still selectable.
claims.contract: ListboxBaseProps.readOnly TSDoc: "Keeps the trigger focusable and the value submitted, but blocks opening and selection." The weaker read-only state blocks every open path; the stronger disabled state does not.
claims.evidence: listbox.tsx lines 224-231: `setOpenGuarded` short-circuits on `resolvedReadOnly` only — `if (resolvedReadOnly && next) return` — and it is what backs the frame click at line 354 (`onClick: () => setOpenGuarded(!open)`). That handler is spread onto `ControlFrame` via `frameProps` (select-trigger.tsx line 72), and the frame is a plain span with no disabled handling: control.tsx lines 20-29 and the `frame` recipe (recipes/kiso/control/frame.ts line 15 = `['relative','group/control',flex.row,'w-full',...layers.all]`) carry no `pointer-events-none`. Clicks on the disabled `<button>` itself are swallowed by the browser, but the chevron lives in a sibling `<span data-slot="suffix">` (select-trigger.tsx lines 80-88) whose clicks bubble to the frame. `resolvedDisabled` comes from useControlProps and is only forwarded to the Button (line 382). Suspected severity: medium-high (a disabled control is operable). Fix: `if ((resolvedReadOnly || resolvedDisabled) && next) return`.

claims.trigger: Wrap a Listbox and an Input in the same `<Field severity="warning">` (or `severity="success"`).
claims.wrongResult: The Input paints the amber warning ring; the Listbox trigger paints nothing. The Listbox emits no `data-warning` / `data-valid` attribute at all, so only the error state ever reaches its chrome.
claims.contract: useControlProps TSDoc @remarks: "`validation` collapses the resolved state into a single spreadable attribute object — invalid wins, then a `warning` / `success` severity — so the three validation rings stay mutually exclusive." Listbox's own comment claims parity: "It also merges the consumer `aria-describedby` with the field's registered ids and resolves `invalid` off the ambient severity, matching Input/Textarea/Slider."
claims.evidence: listbox.tsx lines 190-204 destructure `id, disabled, readOnly, required, invalid, 'aria-describedby'` from `useControlProps` and drop the `validation` member the hook returns. `invalid` is then handed to ListboxButton (line 385) which spreads `invalidAttrs(invalid)` (listbox-button.tsx line 75) — that helper only ever emits the error pair `{'data-invalid':'', 'aria-invalid':true}` (core/invalid-attrs.ts line 1). The sibling control does it the other way: input.tsx line 88 `const validation = invalid === undefined ? sharedAttrs.validation : invalidAttrs(invalid)` and spreads it at line 111, so warning/success reach the ring. Suspected severity: low-medium (visual inconsistency inside one Field). Fix: mirror Input's line — take `validation` off useControlProps and thread it through ListboxButton instead of `invalid`.

claims.trigger: Render a single-select Listbox without a `displayValue` formatter: `<Listbox value={v} onValueChange={setV} placeholder="Select"><ListboxOption value="a">A</ListboxOption></Listbox>` and pick option A.
claims.wrongResult: The trigger keeps showing the placeholder text "Select" forever, even though a value is held. With `clearable` also set, the trigger simultaneously shows the placeholder and a live "Clear selection" button, so the widget claims both empty and non-empty at once.
claims.contract: ListboxProps declares `displayValue?: (value: T) => string` as optional, and the Listbox TSDoc describes the component as a "Select-style dropdown over arbitrary `<ListboxOption>` values: single or `multiple` selection, controlled or uncontrolled" with no statement that the selected label requires a formatter.
claims.evidence: listbox-utilities.ts lines 20-22: `if (value !== undefined && !Array.isArray(value) && displayValue) return displayValue(value)` then `return undefined`. With `displayValue` omitted the single-select arm falls straight through to undefined. listbox.tsx line 289 calls it, line 294 leaves `label` undefined, and listbox-button.tsx line 79 renders `{label || {placeholder}}`. Meanwhile `hasListboxValue` (listbox.tsx lines 116-120) reports true off the same value, so `showClear` on line 298 is true. Note the multi-select arm degrades gracefully to `${arr.length} selected` (line 17); only the single arm has no fallback. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: fall back to `String(value)` in the single arm, or make `displayValue` required by the type when `multiple` is not set. Same-line note: an empty string from `displayValue` also trips the `||` placeholder fallback at listbox-button.tsx line 79.

claims.trigger: Render an uncontrolled Listbox with no `value`, no `defaultValue`, and no `nullable` prop: `<Listbox onValueChange={fn}><ListboxOption value="a">A</ListboxOption></Listbox>`. Select A, then click A again.
claims.wrongResult: The selection clears and `onValueChange(null)` fires, although `nullable` — documented as the opt-in for that behaviour — was never passed. The same markup made controlled (`value={v}`) does the opposite and refuses to clear, so the two modes disagree on a documented behaviour flag.
claims.contract: ListboxBaseProps.nullable TSDoc: "Clicking the selected option clears it." — an opt-in flag, not a default.
claims.evidence: listbox.tsx line 138: `nullable = valueProp == null && defaultValue == null`. In uncontrolled mode `valueProp` is permanently undefined, so the derived default is permanently true and every uncontrolled Listbox is deselectable. In controlled mode it inverts the moment a selection exists: `valueProp` becomes non-null and `nullable` goes false, so the documented clear-on-reclick can never fire for a controlled Listbox that actually holds a value. The flag is therefore true exactly when there is nothing to clear and false exactly when there is. It reaches the behaviour through useListboxState (lines 212-219) into use-deferred-toggle.ts line 55 `if (nullable && prev === newValue) return undefined`. Suspected severity: low-medium (surprising default; controlled/uncontrolled divergence). Fix: default `nullable` to `false` and let callers opt in, as the TSDoc reads.

claims.trigger: Render a `<ListboxOption value="a">A</ListboxOption>` outside any `<Listbox>` (e.g. lifted into a custom panel during a refactor) and click it.
claims.wrongResult: No guard fires at render. The option paints normally as unselected, and the click throws `TypeError: onSelect is not a function` from deep inside the option primitive instead of the named "must be used within" error the context factory promises.
claims.contract: createContext TSDoc: "Without options, the hook throws `use${name} must be used within <${name}>` when used outside a provider; for required context (Menu, Tabs, Dialog, etc.)." and "With `{ default }`, the hook returns the default when used outside a provider … For thin cases where a named hook would be empty sugar, discard the hook and let consumers `use(Context)` directly."
claims.evidence: listbox/context.ts line 12: `export const [ListboxContext] = createContext<ListboxContextValue>('Listbox')` — the guard hook is discarded but no `{ default }` is supplied, so the context's default value is the `MISSING` sentinel Symbol (core/create-context.ts lines 5, 57-59). The only consumer path is `use(config.context)` in primitives/option/option.tsx line 257, which never runs the guard, so destructuring `{ value, multiple, onSelect, capitalize }` off the Symbol yields four `undefined`s; `handleSelect` (line 263) then calls `onSelect(value)`. The factory's own documented example for the discard-the-hook shape pairs it with a default (`createContext<OffcanvasContextValue | null>('Offcanvas', { default: null })`). Suspected severity: low (developer-experience; wrong error surface). Fix: give the context an explicit `{ default }` sentinel and null-check it in the option, or keep the guard hook and read through it.

claims.trigger: Render `<JsonTree data={bigJson} virtualize={{ maxHeight: '20rem' }} defaultExpandDepth={Infinity} />` over a value that flattens to a few thousand rows, Tab into the tree, then press End (or Home from a scrolled position).
claims.wrongResult: Focus lands on the last (or first) row currently inside the rendered window plus overscan, not on the last (or first) item of the tree. ArrowDown past the end of that window wraps back to the top of the window instead of continuing down the tree.
claims.contract: JsonTree TSDoc: "Roving-focus keyboard navigation moves between tree items. Under `virtualize`, flattens the visible tree to a linear list and renders only the viewport slice plus overscan." useA11yRoving TSDoc: "Pass `itemSource` (with `activeIndexRef`) to navigate a windowed list by index instead, reaching items the DOM query can't see."
claims.evidence: json-tree.tsx lines 76-79 build the roving handler with only `{ itemSelector: '[role="treeitem"]', orientation: 'vertical' }` and hand the same handler to the virtualized branch at line 95. The hook then resolves its item set by DOM query — hooks/a11y/use-a11y-roving.ts line 403 `const items = indexed ? [] : queryItems(container, itemSelector)` — and `indexed` is null because no `itemSource`/`activeIndexRef` were supplied (line 401). utilities/keyboard-navigation.ts lines 36-38 compute `Home -> 0` and `End -> itemCount - 1` against that windowed count, and line 65 `wrap(currentIndex + delta, itemCount)` wraps at the window edge. json-tree-virtualized.tsx renders only `virtualItems` (lines 104-117) with DEFAULT_OVERSCAN = 20, so unmounted rows are invisible to the query. Suspected severity: medium (keyboard navigation silently truncated on exactly the large payloads virtualization exists for). Fix: build a VirtualItemSource over `flatNodes` (count, getKey by `${type}:${path}`, scrollToIndex from useVirtualWindow) and pass it with an `activeIndexRef`, as the hook documents.

claims.trigger: Mount a virtualized tree before its payload resolves — `<JsonTree data={payload ?? null} virtualize={{ maxHeight: '20rem' }} defaultExpandDepth={2} />` — then let `payload` arrive from a fetch.
claims.wrongResult: The tree renders a single collapsed root row. `defaultExpandDepth` never applies to the arrived data, unlike the non-virtualized variant, which opens every level below the depth on the same props.
claims.contract: JsonTreeProps.defaultExpandDepth TSDoc: "Nested levels open by default. Pass `Infinity` to expand everything." JsonTreeProps.virtualize TSDoc frames windowing as a rendering strategy only: "Flattens the visible tree into a linear list and renders only the viewport slice plus overscan."
claims.evidence: json-tree-virtualized.tsx lines 49-53 pass `initial: () => collectPaths(data, rootKey, defaultExpandDepth)` into useJsonTreeExpansion, which forwards it as `defaultValue` to useControllable (use-json-tree-expansion.ts line 26). useControllable hands it to `useState(defaultValue)` (hooks/use-controllable.ts line 30), so the thunk is a lazy initializer evaluated exactly once at mount and never re-run when `data` changes. With `data = null`, collectPaths returns an empty Set (json-tree-utilities.tsx line 172 `if (isBranch(data))` is false), so flattenTree's `const open = expanded.has(path)` (line 277) is false for the root and the walk stops there. The recursive path has no equivalent hole: resolveNodeOpen recomputes `depth < defaultExpandDepth` on every render (json-tree-node.tsx line 55). Swapping one object payload for a structurally different one leaves the same stale path set. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: reseed the expanded set in an effect keyed on `data`/`rootKey`/`defaultExpandDepth` when the tree is uncontrolled.

claims.trigger: In a virtualized JsonTree, search for "error" (matching branches auto-expand), manually collapse one of them, clear the search box, then type "error" again.
claims.wrongResult: The second search only highlights. The branch the user collapsed is not re-expanded, so a matching node stays hidden and the search appears to find nothing.
claims.contract: JsonTreeProps.search TSDoc: "Search term to highlight and auto-expand matching nodes." The component TSDoc repeats it: "`search` highlights and auto-expands matching nodes".
claims.evidence: json-tree-virtualized.tsx lines 58-66: `seededSearchRef` is initialised to null and the effect returns early on `if (!searchValue || seededSearchRef.current === searchValue)`. Clearing the box takes the `!searchValue` branch, which returns WITHOUT resetting the ref, so it still holds the previous term; retyping that term hits the equality branch and `expand(collectMatchPaths(...))` never runs. The comment on lines 55-57 states the intent — "Seeds matching branch paths once per search term; a seeded branch stays collapsible afterwards" — but 'once per term' silently means 'once per component lifetime for any repeated term'. The same latch also blocks reseeding when `data` is replaced while the term is unchanged, even though `data` is in the dependency array. Suspected severity: low-medium. Fix: `if (!searchValue) { seededSearchRef.current = null; return }` before the equality check.

claims.trigger: Run a controlled virtualized tree — `<JsonTree data={d} expanded={exp} onExpandedChange={onChange} defaultExpandDepth={Infinity} virtualize={{maxHeight:'20rem'}} />` — where everything is already expanded, then type a search term.
claims.wrongResult: `onExpandedChange` fires with a Set identical to the one the consumer already holds, although the expanded set did not change. A consumer that persists, logs, or diffs on that callback records a change that never happened.
claims.contract: JsonTreeProps.onExpandedChange TSDoc: "Called when the expanded set changes (controlled mode)." The hook's own comment states the intent: "Union `paths` into the expanded set; identity-stable when nothing is new."
claims.evidence: use-json-tree-expansion.ts lines 40-51: the updater correctly returns `base` unchanged when `next.size === base.size`, but useControllable's setter is unconditional about the notification — hooks/use-controllable.ts lines 63-67 run `setInternalValue(normalized)` and then `onValueChangeRef.current?.(normalized ?? null)` with no equality check against the prior value. So the identity-stability guard suppresses the re-render but not the callback. Reached from the search-seeding effect at json-tree-virtualized.tsx line 65. Suspected severity: low. Fix: have `expand` skip the `setExpanded` call entirely when the union adds nothing, e.g. compute the union first and return early.

claims.trigger: Group sibling tree items in a Fragment, which React encourages for a conditional group: `<Tree aria-label="Files">{grouped && <><TreeItem label="a"/><TreeItem label="b"/><TreeItem label="c"/></>}</Tree>`.
claims.wrongResult: All three rows report `aria-posinset="1"` and `aria-setsize="1"`. A screen reader announces every item as "1 of 1", so position and set size are wrong for the whole level.
claims.contract: stampTreePositions TSDoc: "Stamps each element child with its 1-based sibling position via `TreePositionContext`, feeding the items' `aria-posinset`/`aria-setsize`." TreePositionValue TSDoc: "posinset — 1-based position among rendered siblings" / "setsize — Number of rendered siblings at this level."
claims.evidence: tree-item-children.tsx lines 14-32: `Children.toArray(children)` flattens nested arrays but treats a Fragment as one element, so `setsize` (line 16) counts the Fragment as a single sibling and one `TreePositionContext` (lines 26-30) wraps all of its children with `{ posinset: 1, setsize: 1 }`. Every TreeItem beneath it reads the same value through `useTreePosition()` and writes it out at tree-item-content.tsx lines 112-113. The function is used at both levels — tree.tsx line 146 for the root and tree-item-children.tsx line 76 for each group — so the whole tree is exposed. The adjacent falsy-children case is handled (the comment at tree-item.tsx lines 65-68 shows the authors thought about toArray's semantics); the Fragment case was missed. Suspected severity: low-medium (a11y, silent). Fix: unwrap Fragment children before counting, or document Fragments as unsupported at the item level.

claims.trigger: Render a PivotTable with `totals="both"` over a large source set whose values concentrate in few groups — e.g. 300,000 rows pivoted on two distinct row values and two distinct column values, so a single `(row × column)` bucket holds ~75,000 numbers.
claims.wrongResult: The grand-total computation throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` and the whole table fails to render, rather than producing a total.
claims.contract: aggregateAll TSDoc: "Aggregates every value in the grid; `undefined` when it holds none." PivotTableResult.grandTotal TSDoc: "Aggregate over every value in the grid; `undefined` when it holds none." The only documented outcome is a number or undefined.
claims.evidence: pivot-table-pivot.ts line 117: `for (const row of groups.values()) for (const bucket of row.values()) values.push(...bucket)`. Spreading an array into `Function.prototype.apply`-style arguments is bounded by the engine's argument limit (roughly 65k–125k depending on the engine and stack state), and `bucket` is unbounded — groupValues (lines 26-54) pushes one entry per source row into the bucket for its `(row, column)` pair, so bucket size scales with row count divided by the axis cardinality. Reached from use-pivot-table.ts line 87 (`aggregateAll(groups, aggregation)`) on every data change, and rendered at pivot-table.tsx line 155. The sibling reducers avoid the hazard: aggregateRow/aggregateColumn (lines 93, 105) use `flatMap`, which has no argument-count ceiling. Suspected severity: low (needs a large payload) but it is a hard throw, not a degradation. Fix: replace the spread with `for (const v of bucket) values.push(v)`, or accumulate through the same `flatMap` shape the row/column reducers use.

leads.note: `commit` calls `freeze(value)` with the PRE-toggle value before `toggle(newValue)`, so `selectionValue` paints the previously selected row throughout the panel's ~300ms exit animation. The hook TSDoc says the snapshot is "taken at selection time" and "holding the selected row steady during the ~300ms close" — the row that stays steady is the old one, so a single-select Listbox shows the check mark on the wrong option while it closes.

`createSelectOption`'s generated `Option` reads its host state with a bare `use(config.context)` and never guards the result. When the host context was built by `createContext(name)` with no `{ default }`, the value outside a provider is the MISSING sentinel Symbol, which destructures to four undefineds; `handleSelect` then calls `onSelect(value)` and throws a bare TypeError. Applies to every host built on this factory, not just Listbox.

`ControlFrame` accepts and spreads arbitrary props (including `onClick` handed down through `SelectTrigger.frameProps`) but has no disabled handling, and its recipe (recipes/kiso/control/frame.ts) sets no `pointer-events-none`. Any select-family host that routes its open toggle through `frameProps` stays clickable on the frame chrome while its inner control is disabled.

`setValue` fires `onValueChangeRef.current?.(normalized ?? null)` unconditionally, with no comparison against the value already held. Any consumer whose updater deliberately returns the previous value to signal "no change" still emits a change notification — the mechanism behind B06-C14, but it affects every control built on the hook.

claims.trigger: Render `<Alert severity="success" title="Saved" />` conditionally, so the alert mounts already open (the default `defaultOpen` is true) — the ordinary way a success message appears after an action.
claims.wrongResult: Nothing reaches the persistent announcer. The alert's own `role="status"` region is inserted in the same commit as its text, which is exactly the case screen readers drop, so the message is never announced. Only a close-then-reopen of an alert that stayed mounted ever announces.
claims.contract: Alert TSDoc @remarks: "Client component. Polite severities (`info`/`success`, `role="status"`) are re-announced through the persistent announcer on appear, since screen readers can miss a live region inserted together with its text (WCAG 4.1.3); `warning`/`error` use `role="alert"` and announce on insertion."
claims.evidence: alert.tsx L202 `const wasOpen = useRef(open)` seeds the previous-state ref with the *current* open state. The effect at L210-220 computes `const appeared = open && !wasOpen.current`; on the first commit of an already-open alert that is `true && !true === false`, so it returns at L215 before `announce(message)` at L219. The sibling implementation gets this right: toast-alert.tsx L94-101 announces on mount with no closed→open guard. Suspected severity: high (a11y regression against the WCAG 4.1.3 rationale the docblock states, silent for the most common usage). Fix: seed the ref with `false` (`const wasOpen = useRef(false)`), which makes a mount-open count as an appear and leaves the closed→open path unchanged.

claims.trigger: `<Alert severity="error" color="blue">Upload failed</Alert>` — an explicit `color` passed alongside a `severity`.
claims.wrongResult: The `color` prop is discarded: the alert (and its close button) paint the severity's red palette. The same pair of props behaves inconsistently on the icon axis, where an explicit `icon` does override the severity glyph.
claims.contract: AlertProps.severity TSDoc: "Semantic kind: drives the default color, an icon, and the ARIA role (`'alert'` for warning/error, `'status'` for info/success). Use `color` to render a colored alert with no semantic meaning." — a *default* color is by definition overridable.
claims.evidence: alert.tsx L105 `const resolvedColor = severity ? severityColorMap[severity] : (color ?? 'zinc')` puts severity ahead of the explicit prop, while L107 `const resolvedIcon = icon ?? (severity ? severityIconMap[severity] : undefined)` puts the explicit prop ahead of severity. `color` is a real, typed member of `AlertProps` via `AlertVariants` (L61, recipes/kata/alert.ts L15 palette) and is destructured at L166 and threaded to `k({ variant, color: resolvedColor })` at L237 and to the close Button at L256. Suspected severity: low-medium (silent prop drop). Fix: `const resolvedColor = color ?? (severity ? severityColorMap[severity] : 'zinc')`, matching the icon precedence.

claims.trigger: `<form onSubmit={…}><HoldButton type="submit" onHoldComplete={destroy}>Delete</HoldButton></form>` — a caller passing `type`, which the prop type accepts.
claims.wrongResult: The caller's `type` wins over the component's own `type="button"`, so the control becomes a submit button: a single quick click (pointerdown then pointerup, which cancels the hold) fires the native click and submits the form, defeating the hold gate the component exists to enforce.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state, and the resolved wiring of the §7.2 binding cascade — are written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't drop a row out of roving, turn a button into a form submit, or clobber a bound field".
claims.evidence: hold-button.tsx L71-76 renders `<Button type="button" {...props} disabled={disabled} data-slot="hold-button" …>` — `type` is written *before* the spread. `type` survives into `props` because `HoldButtonProps` (L12-15) omits only `href`, `onClick`, and `loading` from `ButtonProps`, and `ButtonProps` carries the native `type` (button.tsx L59-67, L94). Button itself emits whatever `type` it is handed (button.tsx L178) and documents that an untyped button submits (button.tsx L77-80). The in-repo precedent does it correctly: toggle-icon-button.tsx L82-89 spreads `{...props}` first and writes `type="button"` and `aria-pressed` after. Suspected severity: high (irreversible action fires without the hold). Fix: destructure `type` out (or move `type="button"` below `{...props}`).

claims.trigger: `<HoldButton data-slot="delete-hold" onHoldComplete={destroy}>Delete</HoldButton>` — renaming the anchor, which `ButtonProps` explicitly permits.
claims.wrongResult: The custom anchor is silently dropped; the rendered element keeps `data-slot="hold-button"`, so a test or a projection selector written against the caller's name matches nothing.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Presentational attributes stay overridable: a leaf's `data-slot` default is destructured so a consumer can rename the anchor, and `className` merges through `cn`."
claims.evidence: hold-button.tsx L72-75: `{...props}` is spread first and `data-slot="hold-button"` is written after it, so the consumer's value is overwritten. The prop is part of the public surface — button.tsx L50 declares `'data-slot'?: string` on `ButtonBaseProps`, and `HoldButtonProps` (L12-15) does not omit it. Button, Alert, Dialog, and ButtonHeadless all destructure the default instead (button.tsx L95, alert.tsx L177, dialog.tsx L106, button-headless.tsx L31). Note this is the exact inverse ordering error of the `type` attribute two lines up. Suspected severity: low. Fix: destructure `'data-slot': slot = 'hold-button'` and pass `data-slot={slot}`.

claims.trigger: `<Sheet side="top" open onOpenChange={…}>…</Sheet>` on a viewport at or above the `sm` breakpoint, leaving `width` at its default.
claims.wrongResult: The top-docked panel is capped at 28rem and pinned to the left edge instead of spanning the screen, so a full-width banner-style sheet renders as a narrow box in the top-left corner. The same happens for `side="bottom"`.
claims.contract: SheetProps.width TSDoc: "Only on the sides a width is docked across (`right`, `left`). A `top` or `bottom` sheet spans the screen, so it stays full-width."
claims.evidence: sheet.tsx L232 calls `k.panel({ side, width, surface: resolvedSurface })` with `width` unconditioned on `side`. In recipes/kata/sheet.ts the width axis is `width: { ...shaku.panel, fit: [] }` (L57) with `defaults: { side: 'right', width: 'md', surface: 'flat' }` (L71); only the `full` and `fit` values are compounded onto `right`/`left` (L62-69), so the named steps apply on every side. recipes/kiso/shaku/panel.ts L12 resolves `md` to `sm:max-w-md`, and recipes/kiso/narabi/slide.ts L12 gives `top` only `inset-x-0 top-0 w-full` — an over-constrained absolutely positioned box with a max-width resolves to the start edge. A caller cannot opt out from sheet.tsx: the axis has no neutral value (`fit` is empty but is compounded to left/right only). Suspected severity: medium-high (layout break on a documented, supported configuration). Fix: null the width axis for `top`/`bottom` with compounds (`{ side: 'top', width: '*', class: 'sm:max-w-none' }`) or gate the argument in sheet.tsx (`width={panelAxis(side) === 'width' ? width : 'full'}`).

claims.trigger: `<Sheet side="top" handle open>` (or `side="bottom"`) — a resizable sheet docked across the top or bottom edge.
claims.wrongResult: The grab area is drawn over the whole panel rather than as a strip on its inner edge: it stretches from the panel's top to its bottom at `z-10`, so every control inside the sheet is covered by a `role="separator"` that swallows pointer and touch input, and the visible grip bar renders in the middle of the panel instead of on the edge.
claims.contract: SheetHandle TSDoc: "The grab bar on the inner edge of a resizable sheet: a {@link PanelHandle} standing on the edge that faces the screen." — and SheetProps.handle: "Give the panel a drag handle, so the reader can resize it past the `width` scale and throw it away toward its own edge."
claims.evidence: sheet-handle.tsx L40 composes `cn(k.handle.area, k.handle.side[side], className)`. In recipes/kata/sheet.ts the shared area carries `'absolute inset-y-0 z-10 px-3 items-center justify-center'` (L99) — correct for `right`/`left` (L108: `left-0` / `right-0`), but the top/bottom entries only add the opposite edge (L109-110: `'inset-x-0 bottom-0 py-3 w-full'` / `'inset-x-0 top-0 py-3 w-full'`) and never release the inherited `top:0`/`bottom:0`. tailwind-merge does not drop `inset-y-0` here: its conflict map has `inset`/`inset-y` removing earlier `top`/`bottom`, not the reverse, so both declarations survive and the box resolves to top:0;bottom:0;left:0;right:0. `hannou.grab` (L100) adds `touch-none`, so the covering layer also eats touch scrolling. Contrast the drawer, whose grip sits in the flow (recipes/kata/drawer.ts L82-101) and never stretches. Suspected severity: high (a supported configuration renders an unusable panel). Fix: add `top-auto` to the `top` side entry and `bottom-auto` to the `bottom` one, or move `inset-y-0` out of `area` into the `right`/`left` entries.

claims.trigger: `<ShinyText style={{ marginInlineStart: 4 }}>Generating…</ShinyText>` — any caller-supplied `style`, which the prop type accepts through the native `<span>` attributes.
claims.wrongResult: The caller's object replaces the component's entire inline style, dropping `backgroundImage`, `backgroundSize`, and the animated `backgroundPosition` motion value. Because the class list keeps `bg-clip-text text-transparent`, the text then paints transparent over no background and disappears; the sweep stops as well.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Spread order decides what a consumer may override." The file states the same intent for its handlers — "Composed after the spread so a consumer handler can't clobber `pauseOnHover`; both run." — but its load-bearing style is left ahead of the spread.
claims.evidence: shiny-text.tsx L128-132 writes `style={{ backgroundImage: …, backgroundSize: '200% auto', backgroundPosition }}` and L133-136 spreads `{...(props as …)}` after it; `style` reaches `props` because `ShinyTextProps` (L52) omits only `'className'` and `'color'` from `ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'span'>`. The invisibility comes from L124 `'inline-block bg-clip-text text-transparent'` — with no background image the clipped text has nothing to show. `backgroundPosition` is the `useTransform` motion value from L92, so the animation is lost with it. Suspected severity: high (content vanishes from a benign prop). Fix: destructure `style` and merge — `style={{ backgroundImage: …, backgroundSize: …, backgroundPosition, ...style }}` — the same composition the file already applies to `onMouseEnter`/`onMouseLeave` at L137-148.

leads.note: `handle.area` (L94-105) carries `absolute inset-y-0`, and the `handle.side` entries for `top` (L109) and `bottom` (L110) add only the opposite edge, so the grab area resolves to top:0;bottom:0;left:0;right:0 and covers the whole panel. The side entries need `top-auto`/`bottom-auto`, or `inset-y-0` belongs in the `right`/`left` entries only.

The `width` axis (L57, defaults L71) applies `shaku.panel`'s `sm:max-w-*` to every `side`; only `full` and `fit` are compounded to `right`/`left` (L62-69). A `top`/`bottom` sheet therefore caps at `sm:max-w-md` instead of spanning the screen, contradicting the axis comment at L52-56 and the SheetProps.width TSDoc.
`ProgressBarFillVariants` (L106) is exported with no TSDoc and no `@internal` tag, unlike the two neighbours on L104-105 and L107-108; CONVENTIONS.md §12.1 wants one or the other.

claims.trigger: Render `<PdfViewer pages={[{src:'p1.png'},{src:'p2.png'}]} />` with the array written inline (a new array identity per parent render), press Rotate, then cause any unrelated parent re-render (type in a sibling input, tick a timer).
claims.wrongResult: The page snaps back to 0 degrees. Every re-render of the caller wipes the reader's per-page rotations and forces an extra render pass of the whole viewer, because the document identity is taken from the `pages` array reference rather than from anything stable in the page data.
claims.contract: `usePdfViewerPageRotation` TSDoc: "@param documentKey - Identity of the current document; rotations reset when it changes, so a new document starts unrotated." and `PdfViewerProps.pages`: "Pre-rendered page images, in order. When provided, drives what's rendered." — no referential-stability requirement is stated on the prop, and the sibling `highlights` prop explicitly documents the opposite ("Identity need not be stable").
claims.evidence: use-pdf-viewer.ts:340-344 passes `pagesProp ?? src` as the document key; the inline comment claims "consumer-supplied pages carry their own identity", which holds only for a memoized array. use-pdf-viewer-page-rotation.ts:45-51 compares that key with `!==` in render and calls `setRotations({})` on any difference — a fresh `{}` each time, so React cannot bail out and a second render pass runs. Contrast use-pdf-viewer-page-size.ts:33 which keys on `activePage?.id`, a data value, not a reference. Suspected severity: medium — silent loss of reader state on a very common calling pattern. Fix: key on a data-derived identity (`src ?? pages.map(p => p.id ?? p.src).join('|')`) or document `pages` as requiring a stable reference and say so on the prop.

claims.trigger: Mount `<PdfViewer src="/invoice.pdf" />` with nothing resident in the document cache for that `src` (a cold first open).
claims.wrongResult: The first painted frame shows the "No pages to display" empty state instead of the loading placeholder; the skeleton only appears on the following frame. The viewer reports a document with no pages as absent rather than as loading.
claims.contract: `PdfViewerViewport` TSDoc: "Renders the page surface inside the measured viewport: either the active page image … or an error message, a loading placeholder, or an empty state." `usePdfViewer` TSDoc: "When `pages` is omitted but `src` is set, pages are rasterized asynchronously via pdf.js ({@link usePdfViewerDocument}); `loading` and `error` track that lifecycle."
claims.evidence: use-pdf-viewer-document.ts:250-256 — `ensureDocumentLoad` runs in a passive `useEffect`, while `useSyncExternalStore` reads `getDocumentSnapshot(src)` during render. pdf-viewer-document-cache.ts:36-43,186-190 return the frozen `EMPTY` snapshot with `loading: false` for any `src` with no record yet, so the first render commits `loading === false`, `pages === []`, `error === null`. pdf-viewer-viewport.tsx:56-94 then falls through the ternary chain to the final `No pages to display` arm. The publish at pdf-viewer-document-cache.ts:278 (`loading: true`) happens after that commit, and additionally with zero listeners, because the store's subscribe effect is registered after this hook's own effect. Suspected severity: low-medium — a one-frame wrong state on every cold load, exactly the flicker the cache doc claims to remove. Fix: have `getDocumentSnapshot` report `loading: true` for a `src` whose record is absent-but-wanted, or start the load during render as the cache's own docs describe for the hit path.

claims.trigger: With `onActiveHighlightChange` set, press a region ("Total charges"), press `Escape` to clear it, then press the same region again.
claims.wrongResult: Nothing is announced the second time. A screen-reader user hears the region name on the first selection and silence on every re-selection of that same region after a clear, so the selection they just made is unreported.
claims.contract: `PdfViewerHighlights` TSDoc: "A visual box announces nothing on its own. … this says only the name — and only when the regions are in the tree at all". `PdfViewerHighlight.label`: "Accessible name, and what the announcement speaks on activation."
claims.evidence: pdf-viewer-highlights.tsx:119 passes `interactive && activeLabel ? \`Highlighted region: ${activeLabel}\` : null`. hooks/a11y/use-a11y-announcements.ts:30-39 baselines `previous` at the first message and bails on a falsy message *before* updating `previous`, so the `null` between two selections never resets the baseline; the repeated string then equals `previous.current` and is dropped. Reproduces on select A -> clear -> select A. Suspected severity: medium (WCAG 4.1.3). Fix here: give the message a change token (e.g. include the activation count), or fix the hook to record `previous.current = message` on the falsy branch — see the lead.

claims.trigger: Two viewers on one `src` whose first rasterization reported some pages and then threw (a corrupt page mid-document). Viewer A is mounted and showing page 1; mount viewer B on the same `src` (or unmount and remount A).
claims.wrongResult: Viewer A's displayed page image goes blank and the viewer drops back to the loading skeleton for the length of a full re-rasterization: the blob URLs it is currently rendering are revoked and its snapshot is reset to zero pages, even though a listener is holding the entry.
claims.contract: `evict` TSDoc: "Skips anything a viewer is watching … A watched entry's blob URLs are live `` sources, and revoking one blanks the page a reader is looking at — so the holders outrank the cap". `revoke` TSDoc: "A finished snapshot owns no pdf.js resources".
claims.evidence: pdf-viewer-document-cache.ts:269 lets an errored-but-partial entry (`pages.length > 0 && error`) fall past the finished-document guard; line 274 then calls `revoke(held.snapshot)` and line 278 publishes `{ pages: [], documentUrl: null, loading: true }` with no check of `held.listeners.size`, which is the very check `evict` (lines 115-127) is written around. The holder rule is enforced for eviction and not for a retry. Note also that partial-pages-plus-error never surfaces the error at all: pdf-viewer-viewport.tsx:56 takes the image branch whenever `activePage` exists, so the alert arm is unreachable for that state. Suspected severity: medium. Fix: skip the restart (or defer the revoke) while `held.listeners.size > 0`, the same predicate `evict` uses.

claims.trigger: `<Filters aria-label="…"><FiltersField name="done"><Checkbox /></FiltersField></Filters>`; tick the checkbox, then untick it.
claims.wrongResult: The bar reports "1 filter active" and keeps `{ done: false }` in the emitted value, while the checkbox renders exactly as it does when the key is absent. Two states that are indistinguishable on screen produce different active counts and different query payloads, so a clear affordance and an announcement claim a filter the reader has visibly switched off.
claims.contract: `Filters` TSDoc: "Shares set/clear and an active-count through context to enclosed {@link FiltersField} and {@link FiltersClear}, dropping empty fields (undefined, null, `''`, empty array) from the payload so the value stays minimal."
claims.evidence: filters.tsx:24-30 — `isActive(false)` returns true; its own remark concedes "it does read against the 'drops empty fields' contract". filters.tsx:116-121 keeps the key, filters.tsx:135-142 counts it and announces the count. The round trip is closed by filters-field.tsx:82, `{ checked: !!fieldValue }`, which maps both `undefined` (no key) and `false` to the same unchecked box, so the reader has no way to tell the two apart or to get back to the absent state. Suspected severity: low-medium. Fix: either exclude `false` from `isActive` for the toggle path, or have `FiltersField` delete the key when a Checkbox/Switch reports `false`.

claims.trigger: Swap the `pages` prop for a second document whose entries carry no `id` (only `src`), while the viewer sits on page 1 and the pages carry no explicit `width`/`height`.
claims.wrongResult: The viewport keeps the previous document's measured aspect ratio until the new image fires its own load event, so the first document's page shape is reserved for the second document's page — the exact regression the per-page reset exists to prevent.
claims.contract: `usePdfViewerPageSize` TSDoc: "Page change resets the measured size; a new page does not inherit the previous page's aspect ratio while its `` loads." Pinned for id-carrying pages by `pdf-viewer.test.tsx` — "does not size the next page using the previous page's natural dimensions".
claims.evidence: use-pdf-viewer-page-size.ts:33 builds the reset key as `${activePage?.id ?? ''}:${safePage}`; with `PdfViewerPage.id` optional (types.ts:6-7, "Stable key. Falls back to the array index when omitted.") the key collapses to `:1` for every id-less first page, so a document swap leaves `prevResetKey` unchanged and `naturalSize` is not cleared. pdf-viewer-viewport.tsx:67 keys the `` on `activePage.id ?? safePage`, which likewise collapses, so React reuses the element and only re-measures once the new bitmap decodes. Suspected severity: low. Fix: fold `activePage?.src` into the reset key.

claims.trigger: Import this module into a module graph that is not already inside a client boundary — a React Server Component, or a new `ui` entry that re-exports it — and render it.
claims.wrongResult: React throws that hooks cannot be called in a Server Component, because the file calls `useMemo` while carrying no `'use client'` directive; source-level it presents as a static-tier module that renders in RSC.
claims.contract: `packages/ui/REFERENCE.md` §2: "**Static components** carry no `'use client'` directive and read no context, so they render in React Server Components. … **Client components** keep `'use client'` in their own file (per [CONVENTIONS.md] §2.2)". CONVENTIONS.md §2.2: "keep `'use client'` on the interactive leaf".
claims.evidence: pdf-viewer-zoom-controls.tsx:1-2 begins at the `lucide-react` import with no directive, and line 22 calls `useMemo`; lines 30-32 also close over click handlers. Every other `.tsx` in the pdf-viewer directory carries the directive (pdf-viewer.tsx, pdf-viewer-toolbar.tsx, pdf-viewer-toolbar-button.tsx, pdf-viewer-viewport.tsx, pdf-viewer-thumbnails.tsx, pdf-viewer-highlights.tsx, …), so this is an omission rather than a tier choice. `static-component-boundary.test.ts` scans only its own explicit list, which pdf-viewer is not on, so nothing catches it. Suspected severity: low today (the file is only reachable through `PdfViewer`, which is a client component) and latent on any re-export. Fix: add `'use client'` as the first line.

claims.trigger: Render this component from a React Server Component, or from any module graph not already inside a client boundary.
claims.wrongResult: Next.js throws "Event handlers cannot be passed to Client Component props" for the `onClick` handlers it hands to `PdfViewerToolbarButton`; the file has no `'use client'` directive, so it is treated as server-tier while it is unambiguously interactive.
claims.contract: `packages/ui/REFERENCE.md` §2: "**Client components** keep `'use client'` in their own file (per [CONVENTIONS.md] §2.2)." CONVENTIONS.md §2.2: "keep `'use client'` on the interactive leaf; never promote it onto a layout or page that could stay server-rendered."
claims.evidence: pdf-viewer-document-actions.tsx:1 starts at the `lucide-react` import with no directive; lines 26-28 define `download`/`print` closures and lines 32-43 pass them as `onClick`. It also reaches `document`/`window` transitively through `pdf-viewer-utilities.ts`. Suspected severity: low (reachable only through the client-tier toolbar today), latent on re-export. Fix: add `'use client'`.

claims.trigger: Render `<PdfViewer pages={pages} />` and query the rendered tree for `[data-slot="pdf-viewer-page-status"]`.
claims.wrongResult: Two structurally different elements answer the same anchor: the toolbar's visible total-page count and the viewport's visually hidden "Page X of Y" live region. A single-node query silently resolves to whichever comes first in the DOM, so a test or consumer reading "the page status" gets the total count and never the live region.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §10.2: "Component tests render through the library's test renderer and query by `data-slot`. New components expose stable `data-slot` anchors and a filename-matched export."
claims.evidence:
pdf-viewer-viewport.tsx:52 renders `
Page {safePage} of {total}
`; pdf-viewer-toolbar.tsx:109 renders `{total}`. `pdf-viewer.test.tsx` ("shows the total page count") passes only because `bySlot` returns the first match and the toolbar precedes the viewport in the tree. Suspected severity: low. Fix: rename the live region to `pdf-viewer-page-announcement` (or the toolbar span to `pdf-viewer-page-total`).

claims.trigger: Below the `lg` breakpoint, press the toolbar's thumbnails button to open the mobile Sheet, then read the button and press it again.
claims.wrongResult: The button keeps the accessible name "Show thumbnails" while reporting `aria-expanded="true"`, so its name contradicts its state, and pressing it again re-sets the same value instead of closing the Sheet — the control offers an action it has already performed and cannot undo.
claims.contract: `PdfViewerToolbarButton` TSDoc: "every control in this bar keeps its glyph and names the *action* rather than the state ('Hide highlights' while they are shown)". The desktop sibling in the same file follows it: `sidebarOpen ? 'Hide thumbnails' : 'Show thumbnails'`.
claims.evidence: pdf-viewer-toolbar.tsx:55 derives `sidebarToggleLabel` for the desktop control, but lines 77-85 hardcode `label="Show thumbnails"` with `aria-expanded={thumbsOpen}` and `onClick={() => setThumbsOpen(true)}` — a set, not a toggle. `pdf-viewer.test.tsx` ("opens the mobile thumbnails sheet when toggled") asserts exactly this state: `getByLabelText('Show thumbnails')` carries `aria-expanded="true"` after opening. Suspected severity: low-medium (WCAG 4.1.2 name/state mismatch). Fix: mirror the desktop control — `thumbsOpen ? 'Hide thumbnails' : 'Show thumbnails'` with `onClick={() => setThumbsOpen(!thumbsOpen)}`.

claims.trigger: Run the docs surface generation (`pnpm docs`) or any TSDoc extraction over the package, or consult the public-surface indexes for this symbol.
claims.wrongResult: The helper is presented as a public, package-level export: it carries a full doccomment with `@param`/`@returns` and no `@internal` tag, yet no barrel re-exports it and it has no entry in the `packages/ui/docs/*` surface indexes, so the documented surface and the real surface disagree.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §12.1: "`@internal` on a documented helper that no barrel re-exports — the tag and a barrel entry are mutually exclusive".
claims.evidence: pdf-viewer-highlight-geometry.ts:6-21 documents `toFractionRect` with `@param`, `@returns` and `@remarks` and no `@internal`; `pdf-viewer/index.ts:1-14` re-exports only `PdfViewer`, `PdfViewerProps` and the public types. Suspected severity: low. Fix: add `@internal` to the doccomment.

claims.trigger: Run the docs surface generation (`pnpm docs`) or any TSDoc extraction over the package, or consult the public-surface indexes for this symbol.
claims.wrongResult: The helper is presented as a public, package-level export: it carries a full doccomment with `@param`/`@returns` and no `@internal` tag, yet no barrel re-exports it and it has no entry in the `packages/ui/docs/*` surface indexes.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §12.1: "`@internal` on a documented helper that no barrel re-exports — the tag and a barrel entry are mutually exclusive".
claims.evidence: use-pdf-viewer-magnifier.ts:134-152 documents `lensOffset` with `@param`, `@returns`, `@remarks` and no `@internal`, while every neighbouring export in the same file (`MagnifierChoice`, `ResolvedMagnifier`, `MagnifierOption`, `zoomOptions`, `sizeOptions`, `delayOptions`, `resolveMagnifierChoice`, `resolveMagnifier`, `MagnifierPoint`, `PdfViewerMagnifierResult`, `usePdfViewerMagnifier`) does carry the tag; `pdf-viewer/index.ts:1-14` re-exports none of them. leads.note: The baseline ref is not updated on the falsy-message branch: the effect returns early when `message` is null/undefined *before* writing `previous.current`. A caller that alternates message -> null -> the same message (the pdf-viewer highlight overlay does exactly this on select/clear/re-select) gets no announcement for the repeat.

`{...props}` is spread onto the `<input>` after `type="radio"`, `data-slot`, `disabled`, `required` and the resolved `validation` attributes, so a stray prop can change the input type or clobber the widget ARIA state. CONVENTIONS.md §3.9 requires those to be written after the spread.

Same spread-order issue: `{...props}` lands after `type="checkbox"`, `data-slot`, the resolved `validation` attributes and `className`, so a caller-supplied `aria-invalid` or `className` overrides the component's own resolved wiring rather than merging (CONVENTIONS.md §3.9).

claims.trigger: An `<AccordionTrigger>` rendered inside a `<form>` that receives a spread prop bag carrying `type="submit"` (or any explicit `type`), e.g. `<AccordionTrigger {...sharedButtonProps}>Section</AccordionTrigger>`.
claims.wrongResult: The consumer prop wins over the component's own `type="button"`, so clicking the accordion header submits the enclosing form instead of only toggling the section.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state, and the resolved wiring of the §7.2 binding cascade — are written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't drop a row out of roving, turn a button into a form submit, or clobber a bound field". The file's own inline comment also asserts "Consumer props spread first; the a11y id wiring, roving tabindex, context-driven disabled, and data-slot below take precedence."
claims.evidence: accordion-trigger.tsx lines 42-59: `type="button"` is emitted at line 45, BEFORE `{...props}` at line 48. Everything the comment lists (data-slot, triggerProps, aria-controls, disabled, onClick, className) is correctly placed after the spread; `type` alone is above it. Compare `pagination-utilities.tsx` line 14, which has the same ordering problem, and `primitives/polymorphic/fallback.tsx` line 57, which is the shared root of the pattern. Severity: low-medium (a11y/behaviour regression only when a caller spreads a prop bag, but §3.9 names this exact failure). Fix: move `type="button"` below `{...props}`, beside `data-slot`.

claims.trigger: `<Accordion mount="always"><AccordionItem value="a"><AccordionTrigger>A</AccordionTrigger><AccordionPanel>…</AccordionPanel></AccordionItem>…</Accordion>` with section `a` closed (also reproduces under `mount="lazy"` after the section has been opened once).
claims.wrongResult: The closed section's header button carries no `aria-controls`, although its panel element (with the matching id) is present in the DOM inside a hidden `<Activity>`. Assistive technology loses the trigger→panel relation the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern requires, and the reason given in the source (the panel is unmounted) is false for these policies.
claims.contract: `primitives/mount/mount.ts` TSDoc on `mountsEveryPanel`: "Whether a policy guarantees every panel is in the DOM — the question a trigger asks before pointing `aria-controls` at a panel it doesn't render. Only `always` can answer yes: `lazy` mounts panels as they are visited, which no sibling trigger can observe, and `active` keeps just the one." The exported helper exists for this decision and the trigger never calls it.
claims.evidence: accordion-trigger.tsx lines 50-53: `aria-controls={open ? triggerProps['aria-controls'] : undefined}` with the comment "The panel unmounts while closed (AnimatePresence); the reference is set only while its target id exists." That premise holds only for `mount='active'`. accordion.tsx lines 35, 69, 81-90 put `mount` on the context; accordion/context.ts line 10 types it; accordion-panel.tsx lines 40, 64-82 renders `<Hold hold={hold} name="accordion-panel">` whenever `hold.held`, and `primitives/mount/hold.tsx` lines 28-36 wraps it in `<Activity mode="hidden">`, which per its own TSDoc "keeps its subtree in the DOM at `display: none` with state intact". `useMountHold` (mount.ts line 114) returns `present: mount === 'always' || active || (mount === 'lazy' && everActive.current)`. `Tabs` already solves the same problem the other way (tabs.tsx lines 56-68, `panelsMounted` ref-count "so inactive tabs keep aria-controls"). Severity: medium (a11y). Fix: read `mount` from `useAccordion()` and gate on `open || mountsEveryPanel(mount)`, or adopt the Tabs ref-count so `lazy` is covered too.

claims.trigger: `<Collapse mount="always"><CollapseTrigger>Details</CollapseTrigger><CollapsePanel>…</CollapsePanel></Collapse>` while closed.
claims.wrongResult: The trigger renders without `aria-controls` even though the panel `<section>` with that id is in the DOM (hidden `<Activity>`), so the disclosure relation is missing for assistive technology in exactly the mount mode that guarantees the target exists.
claims.contract: `primitives/mount/mount.ts` TSDoc on `mountsEveryPanel`: "Whether a policy guarantees every panel is in the DOM — the question a trigger asks before pointing `aria-controls` at a panel it doesn't render. Only `always` can answer yes". The component's own TSDoc also promises "`aria-controls` only while the panel is mounted", which is the opposite of what the code computes.
claims.evidence: collapse-trigger.tsx lines 17-31: destructures only `{ open, toggle, triggerProps }` from `useCollapseContext()` and sets `aria-controls={open ? triggerProps['aria-controls'] : undefined}` with the comment "The panel unmounts while closed (AnimatePresence)". collapse/context.ts line 13 exposes `mount` on the very context the trigger already reads; collapse.tsx lines 47, 68, 92-103 puts it there. collapse-panel.tsx lines 38, 69-101 keeps the panel mounted under `<Hold>` for `always`/`lazy`. Severity: medium (a11y). Fix: pull `mount` off the context and use `open || mountsEveryPanel(mount)`.

claims.trigger: `<form><Collapse><CollapseTrigger {...buttonPropsFromCaller}>More</CollapseTrigger>…</Collapse></form>` where the spread bag contains `type="submit"`.
claims.wrongResult: The consumer's `type` overrides the component's `type="button"`, so opening the disclosure submits the surrounding form.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state … are written *after* `{...props}`, so a stray prop can't … turn a button into a form submit".
claims.evidence: collapse-trigger.tsx lines 20-36: `type="button"` at line 22 precedes `{...props}` at line 26; every other guarded attribute (data-slot, triggerProps, aria-controls, onClick, className) correctly follows it. Severity: low-medium. Fix: move `type="button"` below the spread.

claims.trigger: `<Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>T</CardTitle></CardHeader><CardBody>body</CardBody></Card>`.
claims.wrongResult: The header keeps its projected bottom padding instead of collapsing to zero, so header and body do not sit flush — the documented "header directly followed by a body" special case never fires, at any `size`.
claims.contract: CardHeader TSDoc: "A {@link CardBody} as its next sibling collapses that gap to zero, so the two sit flush; any other next sibling (or none) keeps the projected gap." Card TSDoc: "A header directly followed by a body collapses that gap to zero — the two sit flush."
claims.evidence: card.tsx line 48 composes the projection set: `cn('overflow-hidden -outline-offset-1', k.slots[step], className)`. `recipes/kata/card.ts` lines 14-30 defines `slots` as only `['*:data-[slot=card-header]:pb-2|3|4', '*:data-[slot=card-footer]:pt-2|3|4', '*:data-[slot=card-footer]:gap-1|2|3']` — there is no `:has(+[data-slot=card-body])` (or equivalent) rule anywhere, and `k.header` (line 41) is `text.default`, a colour pair only (`recipes/kiso/iro/text.ts`). card-body.tsx line 15 is `createSlot('div','card-body')` with no compensating negative margin either. So the documented collapse is unimplemented. Severity: medium (visible spacing bug on the most common Card composition, plus a false public doc). Fix: add `'*:data-[slot=card-header]:has(+[data-slot=card-body]):pb-0'` to each `slots` row, or drop the promise from both TSDocs.

claims.trigger: `<AvatarGroup><Avatar src="a.png" status="active" /><Avatar src="b.png" /></AvatarGroup>` — any child Avatar that also passes `status`.
claims.wrongResult: The white separator ring is painted as a square around the status wrapper instead of a circle around the avatar, and the avatar circle itself gets no ring at all, so the overlapping avatars visually merge.
claims.contract: AvatarGroup TSDoc: "Overlapping row of avatars. … The group projects its `size` onto descendant avatars, so children need no size of their own." packages/ui/REFERENCE.md §2: "AvatarGroup projects descendant avatar sizes."
claims.evidence: avatar-group.tsx lines 22-29 composes `k.group.ring` alongside `k.group.size[size]`. In `recipes/kata/avatar.ts`, `ring` (line 33) is `'*:ring-2 *:ring-white dark:*:ring-zinc-900'` — a direct-child (`& > *`) selector — while `size` (lines 45-49) is `'**:data-[slot=avatar]:size-7|9|11'`, a descendant selector whose own comment says it exists because `**:` "reaches an avatar inside its with-status wrapper". avatar.tsx lines 84-107 shows the status path renders `<span data-slot="avatar-with-status" className={cn('relative inline-flex', …)}>` as the direct child, with the round `data-slot="avatar"` span nested inside. `relative inline-flex` carries no border radius, so `ring-2` traces a rectangle. Severity: medium (visual). Fix: key the ring on `**:data-[slot=avatar]` the way the size row already is.

claims.trigger: `<AvatarGroup size="lg"><Avatar src="a.png" status="active" /></AvatarGroup>`.
claims.wrongResult: The avatar circle grows to the `lg` box but its corner status dot stays at the `md` dot size, so the indicator is visibly under-scaled (and over-scaled for `size="sm"`), contradicting the promise that children need no size of their own.
claims.contract: AvatarGroup TSDoc: "The group projects its `size` onto descendant avatars, so children need no size of their own." packages/ui/REFERENCE.md §2: "AvatarGroup projects descendant avatar sizes. … Direct-child and exact-depth selectors keep nested instances independent."
claims.evidence: avatar-group.tsx lines 22-29 projects only `k.group.spacing[size]` and `k.group.size[size]`. `recipes/kata/avatar.ts` lines 45-49: the only projected selector is `**:data-[slot=avatar]:size-*`; nothing targets `data-slot="status-dot"`. avatar.tsx line 39 fixes `resolvedSize = size ?? 'md'` and line 101 passes `size={resolvedSize}` to `<StatusDot>`; both Avatar and StatusDot are static leaves (avatar.tsx has no `'use client'`; status-dot.tsx none either), so no context can correct it — REFERENCE §2 requires the correction to travel through the DOM projection, which is missing. StatusDot forwards to `Swatch`, whose size compounds are `size-1.5 … size-4` (`recipes/kata/swatch.ts` lines 44-59), so the mismatch is visible. Severity: low-medium (visual). Fix: add `**:data-[slot=status-dot]` rows (and a matching `statusRing` row) to the group's size projection.

claims.trigger: The first `loadShiki()` call in a session rejects — an offline chunk fetch, or a post-deploy 404 on the `shiki` chunk. Then the network recovers and the user navigates to another page with a `<CodeBlock>`, or remounts the same one.
claims.wrongResult: Every later `CodeBlock` in that session stays on the unstyled `<pre>` fallback forever. The memoised promise is a rejected one, so no retry is ever attempted and nothing short of a full page reload recovers.
claims.contract: loadShiki TSDoc: "Dynamically imports the Shiki highlighter on first call, memoizing the in-flight promise so the heavy module is fetched at most once per session." A rejected promise is not in flight. The CodeBlock effect's own comment states the intent: "Shiki can fail to load (offline chunk fetch, post-deploy 404) … Keep the plain fallback … rather than leaking an unhandled rejection and stranding the component with no recovery."
claims.evidence: code-block.tsx lines 38-53: `let shikiPromise: Promise<typeof import('shiki')> | null = null; export function loadShiki() { if (!shikiPromise) { shikiPromise = import('shiki') } return shikiPromise }`. Nothing clears `shikiPromise` on rejection, so the `.catch(() => {})` at line 133 silently swallows the same rejection on every subsequent mount. The stated goal at lines 129-133 ("stranding the component with no recovery") is exactly what happens. Severity: medium. Fix: `shikiPromise = import('shiki').catch((error) => { shikiPromise = null; throw error })`.

claims.trigger: `<CodeBlock code={snippetWithLinesWiderThanTheContainer} />` — any snippet whose longest line overflows the block horizontally.
claims.wrongResult: The horizontally scrollable region cannot be reached or scrolled by keyboard: nothing in the block is focusable, so a keyboard-only or screen-reader user cannot read the clipped part of the code (axe `scrollable-region-focusable` / WCAG 2.1.1).
claims.contract: CodeBlock TSDoc: "The highlighted `<pre>` is made non-focusable (`tabindex="-1"`) to keep scroll containers out of the tab order." The library's own rule for the same situation is the opposite — scroll-area.tsx: "Keyboard-focusable on any enabled axis (axe scrollable-region-focusable). tabIndex is omitted when no axis is enabled" with `tabIndex={hasVertical || hasHorizontal ? 0 : undefined}`.
claims.evidence: code-block.tsx line 142 renders the scroll container `<div className={cn(k.block.content)}>` — `recipes/kata/code.ts` line 26 defines `block.content` as `['min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-x-auto', size.sm]`, so this div is the scroller and it carries no `tabIndex`. Lines 116-121 install a shiki transformer that overwrites shiki's default `tabindex="0"` with `node.properties.tabindex = '-1'`, and line 149 does the same for the plain fallback `<pre className={cn(k.block.fallback)} tabIndex={-1}>`. Both branches therefore leave the overflow container out of the tab order. Severity: medium (a11y, WCAG 2.1.1). Fix: put `tabIndex={0}` (with a `role="region"` + label, mirroring ScrollArea) on the `k.block.content` div, or drop the transformer and let shiki's `tabindex="0"` stand on a `<pre>` that owns the overflow.

claims.trigger: A live bar sparkline whose series grows a point: `<Sparkline animate variant="bar" data={series} aria-label="Requests" />` re-rendered with `series` one element longer (a polling dashboard cell).
claims.wrongResult: Every bar unmounts and remounts, so the whole chart replays its staggered grow-from-baseline entrance on each update instead of only the new bar animating in; the existing bars flicker back to zero height.
claims.contract: SparklineProps.animate TSDoc: "Animate the marks in on mount with Framer Motion: … bars rise from the baseline in sequence." The entrance is specified as an on-mount effect, not something a data append should replay for already-drawn bars.
claims.evidence: sparkline.tsx line 161 `<motion.rect key={bar.x} … initial={{ y: geometry.baseline, height: 0 }} animate={{ y: bar.y, height: bar.height }} transition={{ ...k.motion.grow, delay: index * k.motion.stagger }} />` (and line 103 `<rect key={bar.x}>` in the static path). `sparkline-geometry.ts` lines 138-158 computes `slot = innerWidth / data.length` and `x = padding + index * slot + (slot - barWidth) / 2`, so `bar.x` is a function of `data.length`: appending one datum shifts every bar's x and therefore every React key. A secondary case of the same key choice: with `width` small enough that `innerWidth` clamps to 0 (line 68 `Math.max(0, width - padding * 2)`), `slot` is 0 and every bar shares one key, producing duplicate-key warnings and dropped rects. Severity: medium (visual/perf on live charts). Fix: key on the datum index (`key={index}`) or a caller-supplied key, not on derived geometry.

claims.trigger: `<Avatar alt="Ada Lovelace" />` — an avatar with neither `src` nor `initials` (a record whose photo and initials are both unavailable).
claims.wrongResult: The `alt` text is silently discarded: an empty circle renders with no image, no text, and no accessible name, so assistive technology announces nothing at all for the avatar.
claims.contract: Avatar TSDoc: "User image, initials, or fallback in a sized circle." The `alt` prop is part of the public `AvatarProps` surface and is the only accessible-name channel the component offers.
claims.evidence: avatar.tsx lines 43-69: `alt` reaches the DOM in exactly two places — as the initials `` (line 67, only when `src` is truthy). With both absent, `content` is an empty fragment and the outer `` (lines 73-80) has no name, no role, and no children. The `initialsHidden = !!src || !alt` expression at line 43 confirms `alt` is treated purely as a companion to the two content sources. Severity: low-medium (a11y; silent prop drop). Fix: render the `alt` in an `sr-only` span (the same technique the status branch already uses at line 105) when no visible content is produced, or make the fallback content explicit.

claims.trigger: A component test or consumer that renders `<PaginationSkeleton />` and queries its root, e.g. `renderUI(<PaginationSkeleton />)` then `getByTestSlot('pagination-skeleton')` / `container.querySelector('[data-slot]')` on the root element.
claims.wrongResult: There is no queryable anchor: the root `<div>` carries no `data-slot`, so the only matches inside the tree are the inner `data-slot="placeholder"` nodes and the skeleton root itself cannot be selected or asserted on.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §10.2: "Component tests render through the library's test renderer and query by `data-slot`. New components expose stable `data-slot` anchors and a filename-matched export."
claims.evidence: pagination-skeleton.tsx lines 24-30: `<div className={cn(k(), className)}>` with no `data-slot`, while every sibling in the same directory anchors itself — pagination.tsx line 15 `data-slot="pagination"`, pagination-list.tsx line 13 `data-slot="pagination-list"`, pagination-gap.tsx line 13 `data-slot="pagination-gap"`, pagination-page.tsx line 40 `data-slot="pagination-page"`. The symbol is public (`pagination/index.ts` line 8). Severity: low. Fix: add `data-slot="pagination-skeleton"` to the root div.

claims.trigger: `<Divider orientation="vertical" role="presentation" />`, or a vertical divider rendered from a shared attribute bag that happens to carry `role` or `aria-orientation` (e.g. `<Divider orientation="vertical" {...slotProps} />`).
claims.wrongResult: The consumer prop silently replaces the component's computed separator semantics, so the vertical rule reports the wrong role or the wrong orientation to assistive technology while still painting as a vertical separator.
claims.contract: CONVENTIONS.md §3.9: "Load-bearing structural attributes — `role`, `tabIndex`, `type`, widget ARIA state, and the resolved wiring of the §7.2 binding cascade — are written *after* `{...props}` … Presentational attributes stay overridable". Divider's own TSDoc calls these load-bearing: "The `vertical` orientation adds `role=\"separator\"` and `aria-orientation=\"vertical\"` for assistive tech".
claims.evidence: divider.tsx lines 21-28: `role={orientation === 'vertical' ? 'separator' : undefined}` (line 24) and `aria-orientation={…}` (line 25) are both emitted before `{...props}` at line 27. `DividerProps` (lines 6-8) widens to `Omit<ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'hr'>, 'className'>`, which includes both attributes, so the override path is reachable. Severity: low. Fix: move `role` and `aria-orientation` below the spread, keeping `data-slot` and `className` above it as presentational.

claims.trigger: A caller following the component TSDoc writes `<StatDelta trend="flat">0%</StatDelta>`.
claims.wrongResult: `flat` is not a member of the trend axis, so the call fails typecheck; the documented third state is spelled `neutral` in the recipe and nowhere in the doc.
claims.contract: StatDelta TSDoc: "Period-over-period change indicator, tinted by `trend` (up/down/flat)."
claims.evidence: stat-delta.tsx lines 10-18 name the values `up/down/flat`; `StatDeltaVariants` is `VariantProps<typeof delta>` and `recipes/kata/stat.ts` lines 28-36 define the axis as `trend: { up, down, neutral }` with `defaults: { trend: 'neutral' }`. `turbo run check-types` fails on the documented call. Severity: low (doc/API mismatch on a public export; §12.1 requires the TSDoc to describe the surface). Fix: change the TSDoc to `(up/down/neutral)`.

claims.trigger: Render an `<Accordion>` with three `<AccordionItem>`s and press Tab repeatedly from a control placed before it.
claims.wrongResult: Focus stops on every header button in turn rather than entering the accordion once and leaving it on the next Tab, so the widget is three tab stops, not the single roving one the documentation promises.
claims.contract: Accordion TSDoc @remarks: "Triggers share a roving tabindex: Arrow keys move focus between enabled header buttons, skipping disabled ones." AccordionItemProps.disabled TSDoc: "Prevents toggling and removes the trigger from roving-tabindex navigation."
claims.evidence: accordion.tsx lines 94-96 call `useA11yRoving(ref, { itemSelector: '[data-slot="accordion-trigger"]:not(:disabled)' })` and pass no `manageTabIndex`. `hooks/a11y/use-a11y-roving.ts` line 861 defaults `manageTabIndex = false`, and its TSDoc states the flag is what makes the hook "own the roving `tabIndex` so the widget is a single Tab stop. Seats `tabIndex=0` on the resting item … and `-1` on the rest"; the effect at lines 883-953 short-circuits without it. Native `<button>`s therefore all stay tabbable (accordion-trigger.tsx line 44 never sets `tabIndex`). Only the arrow-key handler is wired. Severity: low (the behaviour matches the APG accordion pattern, so the defect is the public contract, not necessarily the code — one of the two must move). Fix: either delete "roving tabindex" from both TSDocs and describe arrow-key navigation over individually tabbable headers, or pass `manageTabIndex: true`.

leads.note: The AvatarGroup projection set is inconsistent in selector depth: `group.ring` (line 33) uses the direct-child variant `*:ring-2 *:ring-white`, while `group.size` (lines 45-49) uses the descendant variant `**:data-[slot=avatar]:size-*` precisely because, per its own comment, `**:` is needed to reach "an avatar inside its with-status wrapper". The ring therefore lands on the un-rounded `data-slot=avatar-with-status` span. There is also no projected row for `data-slot=status-dot`, so a non-md group leaves the corner dot at its md size.

`slots` (lines 14-30) carries only header `pb-*`, footer `pt-*`, and footer `gap-*`. It has no rule collapsing the header's bottom padding when a `data-slot=card-body` is its next sibling, although both `card.tsx` and `card-header.tsx` document that collapse as guaranteed behaviour. A `*:data-[slot=card-header]:has(+[data-slot=card-body]):pb-0` row per size step is the missing piece.

`renderFallback` writes `type={as === 'button' ? 'button' : undefined}` at line 57, before `{...rest}` at line 59. Every polymorphic button in the library (PaginationPage, Group's button arm, and any future `as="button"` host) can therefore be flipped to a form submit by a stray consumer `type` prop — the exact failure CONVENTIONS.md §3.9 names. This is the shared root of the same ordering issue reported separately for accordion-trigger.tsx and collapse-trigger.tsx.

`PaginationNavButton` (line 14) writes `type="button"` and `variant="plain"` before `{...props}`, so PaginationNext/PaginationPrevious can be turned into form-submit buttons by a spread prop (CONVENTIONS.md §3.9). The file is in scope B07's list, but the symbol is `@internal` and not barrelled, so the reachable trigger runs through pagination-next.tsx / pagination-previous.tsx.

claims.trigger: Render any component that calls `useSortableSensors()` (keyboard sensor on by default) and let its parent re-render for any reason.
claims.wrongResult: `useSensors` returns a brand-new `SensorDescriptor[]` on every render, so `<DndContext>`'s combined-activator memo busts and every sortable item is handed a fresh `listeners` object each render — exactly the churn the pointer sensor's module-scope options object was hoisted to prevent, so the pointer half of the fix is defeated by the keyboard half.
claims.contract: TSDoc on the pointer options constant: "Held as the whole options object, at module scope, because `useSensor` memoises on option identity — a fresh literal per render misses that memo and hands `<DndContext>` a new sensor array every time."
claims.evidence: use-sortable-sensors.ts:52 hoists POINTER_ACTIVATION to module scope for this exact reason, but :83-85 builds `{ coordinateGetter: keyboardCoordinateGetter }` as an inline literal inside the hook body, and :87 spreads both into `useSensors`. Verified in packages/ui/node_modules/@dnd-kit/core/dist/core.esm.js: `useSensor` at :190-196 memoises on `[sensor, options]` (object identity); `useSensors` at :198-205 memoises on `[...sensors]`; `useCombineActivators` at :1933-1943 memoises on `sensors` and is called at :3203, so a new array rebuilds every draggable's synthetic listeners. Downstream, use-sortable-list.ts:129-138 lists `sensors` in the `dndContextProps` memo, so that object is new every render too. Suspected severity: medium (identity churn / lost memoisation across every sortable row; no crash). Fix: hoist a module constant for the default-getter case, or `useMemo` the options on `[keyboardCoordinateGetter]`.

claims.trigger: Render a server-rendered page whose client component calls `useInView()` and gates content on the returned `inView`.
claims.wrongResult: The server emits the gated content (the hook reports true there) while the client's very first render computes false, so hydration mismatches on that subtree and the content is torn out and re-inserted only once the observer fires — the flash the hook exists to avoid.
claims.contract: TSDoc `@remarks`: "Reports `true` where `IntersectionObserver` is not available — server rendering, and jsdom. That is deliberate: the hook gates work that is otherwise correct, so the safe answer when the environment cannot tell is 'show it'."
claims.evidence: use-in-view.ts:61 seeds the flag with `useState(() => typeof IntersectionObserver === 'undefined')`, a lazy initializer that runs during the hydration render on the client and therefore yields `false` where the server yielded `true`. The sibling hook that makes the same "defaults to true during SSR" promise reaches it correctly: use-media-query.ts:12 uses `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, () => true)`, and React consumes `getServerSnapshot` during hydration, so no mismatch. Suspected severity: medium (React hydration error plus a visible content flash for every SSR consumer). Fix: move the flag to `useSyncExternalStore` with a `() => true` server snapshot, mirroring `useMediaQuery`.

claims.trigger: Call `useFloatingUI({ role: 'tooltip', open, ... })` for a tooltip that opens inside a Dialog or Sheet, then press Escape while the tooltip is up.
claims.wrongResult: The tooltip occupies a slot on the shared dismiss stack, so it swallows the Escape press meant for the surface beneath: the tooltip closes and the Dialog stays open, and while the tooltip is up no other surface can be the top layer.
claims.contract: `useEscapeLayer`'s `layered` TSDoc: "Layered surfaces (the default) occupy a slot on the shared dismiss stack, and Escape dismisses only the topmost open surface. Pass `false` for incidental surfaces (tooltips) that close on any Escape press without consuming it for the surface beneath."
claims.evidence: use-floating-ui.ts:401 admits `'tooltip'` into the role union, but :442-445 calls `useEscapeLayer({ open, onDismiss })` with `layered` left at its `true` default (use-escape-layer.ts:37). The disclosure-level twin gets it right: use-floating-disclosure.ts:150-155 passes `layered: roleProp !== 'tooltip'` with a comment naming the same hazard ("Tooltips stay unlayered: incidental hover surfaces close on any Escape without swallowing the press meant for the layer below"). Suspected severity: medium (a11y / dismissal correctness for stacked surfaces). Fix: pass `layered: roleProp !== 'tooltip'` here too.

claims.trigger: Drive virtual-mode roving over DOM items without passing `activeDescendantRef` (the option is documented as optional), leaving `ariaSelected` at its default.
claims.wrongResult: `aria-selected` is never written on any item, so the highlight the helper promises to mirror into selection never reaches assistive technology; the indexed counterpart writes it unconditionally, so two code paths over the same list disagree about whether the highlight is a selection.
