groups.cause: The two pure arithmetic helpers the pdf-viewer directory exports for its jsdom-safe test seam are the only documented, unbarrelled symbols in their files that carry no `@internal` tag, and no gate scans `components` for the omission.

The two interactive pdf-viewer sub-components that carry no `'use client'` directive while every other client-tier file in the directory does — refuted, because no module graph outside a client boundary can reach either.

The document cache is the single source of what a mounted viewer paints, and two of its transitions report a wrong state to a live subscriber: a subscribed-but-unstarted `src` reports absent rather than loading, and a retry on an errored entry revokes and empties a snapshot a viewer is holding.

The viewer has no single document identity, so the two per-document reset hooks called two lines apart each invent their own key and each gets it wrong in a different direction: rotation keys on the `pages` array reference (too volatile), page size keys on page id plus index (not unique across a swap).

steps.change: Give the viewer one document identity and hand it to both reset hooks, replacing `pagesProp ?? src` as the rotation key and the `id:index` string as the page-size key. Update `PdfViewerProps.pages` TSDoc to say what the viewer takes as document identity, since the sibling `highlights` prop states its own stability rule.
steps.order: First. It changes the signature of the two hooks that `use-pdf-viewer.ts` calls on adjacent lines, so any later edit to that file rebases onto it; and the existing page-size test is the only pin either hook has.
steps.seam: Present. Both hooks are pure state hooks with no third-party lifecycle: `renderHook` plus `rerender` drives the document swap and the parent re-render directly, and `pdf-viewer.test.tsx:254-276` already exercises the page-size reset through `renderUI`/`rerender` with `pages` props and no pdfjs.

steps.change: Make the cache report a live subscriber's true state: distinguish a registered-but-unstarted `src` from an absent one for the first frame, and stop the errored-entry retry from revoking and emptying a snapshot whose `listeners` set is non-empty.
steps.order: Second. Independent of S1, but it may move the viewport's branch order, which S3 also touches — running it before S3 keeps `pdf-viewer-viewport.tsx` to one edit.
steps.seam: Present, and already built for this. `ensureDocumentLoad(src, run)` takes the rasterizer as a parameter (`pdf-viewer-document-cache.ts:253`), so a fake `run` that calls `report.page(...)` once and then rejects drives the whole partial-then-throw path with no pdfjs, no fetch and no worker; `resetDocumentCache()` and `documentCacheState()` (`:314`, `:327`) exist for exactly this and give the holder count the assertion needs. §10.3 is satisfied without touching pdfjs.

steps.change: Give the toolbar's total-page count and the viewport's "Page X of Y" live region distinct `data-slot` anchors, so each is addressable by a single-node query.
steps.order: Third, after S2, because S2 may rewrite the viewport branch that hosts one of the two nodes and both edits land in the same file.
steps.seam: Present. A pure jsdom render with `pages` props and `allBySlot`; no third-party lifecycle is involved.

steps.change: Make the highlight announcement speak again when the same region is re-selected after a clear, so a selection is never silent.
steps.order: Fourth. Independent of S1-S3 in files, but gated on a question whose answer decides whether the change stays inside this scope's file list or reaches a shared hook every component uses.

The synchronous seam is the overlay's own state hook: `usePdfViewerHighlights` returns `activate`, `clear` and `activeLabel` (`use-pdf-viewer-highlights.ts:217-225`), and the suite already reaches it directly (`pdf-viewer.test.tsx:3-4` imports `usePdfViewerHighlightsContext` and `PdfViewerHighlightsProvider`), so activate → clear → activate can be driven and the announced string asserted without the layer.

steps.change: Bring the mobile thumbnails control into line with the toolbar-button contract: either flip its name with `thumbsOpen` and close on the second press, or stop stamping `aria-expanded` and keep it a pure opener.
steps.order: Fifth. It touches `pdf-viewer-toolbar.tsx`, which S3 also touches, so it follows S3; and the existing mobile test queries the button by the label this step may change.

Nothing gates a `components` helper that omits the tag, so this step lands unpinned unless the scan is widened — which is a decision for the caller, not a change I propose here.

openQuestions.question: Q1 — What is the viewer's document identity when the consumer supplies `pages`?
openQuestions.axes: Referential stability required and documented on the prop; or derived from the page data (the first page's `src`/`id`, or a joined digest of them); or an explicit `documentKey` prop the consumer owns.
openQuestions.changes: Stability-required turns S1 into a TSDoc change plus an audit of every `pages` call site, and puts it in tension with the sibling `highlights` waiver at `pdf-viewer.tsx:66-68`. Derived changes both hook signatures and adds an O(pages) pass per render that the highlights hook already accepts for itself. An explicit prop adds public surface and so pulls in CONVENTIONS §12.2 (a docs index touch) with the change.

openQuestions.question: Q2 — Where does "loading" begin for a cold `src`?
openQuestions.axes: At subscription, so a registered-but-unfilled entry reports loading from the first render; or in the viewport's branch order, so `src` present with no pages and no error paints the placeholder while `loading` keeps meaning "a run is in flight".
openQuestions.changes: The first edits `pdf-viewer-document-cache.ts` and the frozen `EMPTY` singleton whose identity the hook's server snapshot depends on (`:49-52` states the hydration requirement), so it must answer for the server render. The second confines S2's first half to `pdf-viewer-viewport.tsx` and leaves the cache's vocabulary alone.

openQuestions.question: Q3 — Does a retry on an errored entry defer to the viewers holding it?
openQuestions.axes: Skip the revoke and the reset while `listeners.size > 0` and append to the partial pages; or reset without revoking, leaving the URLs to the evictor; or refuse the retry entirely while a holder is rendering the partial pages, and retry only on a cold subscribe.
openQuestions.changes: The first two decide whether a partially-rasterized document can briefly show its pages twice — the case `pdf-viewer-document-cache.ts:272-274` says the revoke exists to prevent. The third narrows the recovery path the `ensureDocumentLoad` TSDoc promises at `:248-250` ("the next mount retries") and must say what a held error recovers by instead.

openQuestions.question: Q4 — Which node keeps the `pdf-viewer-page-status` name?
openQuestions.axes: The toolbar's total count keeps it (the existing assertion at `pdf-viewer.test.tsx:62` stands, the live region takes a new name); or the viewport's live region keeps it, as the node the name describes (the toolbar count takes a new name and the test moves).
openQuestions.changes: Decides which file S3's rename lands in and whether the existing test changes; it also decides which anchor a future consumer's muscle memory finds, since the name reads as the live region's while the query returns the count.

openQuestions.question: Q5 — Does the re-announce fix land at the call site or in `useA11yAnnouncements`?
openQuestions.axes: The hook records a null message so a return to the same string speaks again — one edit, reaching every caller in the package; or the call site varies what it hands the hook, contained but re-stating the dedupe rule locally.
openQuestions.changes: The hook answer takes S4 outside this scope's file list into `packages/ui/src/hooks/a11y/`, changes behaviour for every other caller (see the lead), and is a cross-component decision the caller may want as its own probe. The call-site answer keeps S4 inside B08 and closes the row alone.

openQuestions.question: Q6 — Is the mobile thumbnails control a disclosure toggle or an opener?
openQuestions.axes: A toggle, matching the desktop sibling at `pdf-viewer-toolbar.tsx:55` and the button's own TSDoc; or an opener that stamps no `aria-expanded`, which the same TSDoc explicitly allows (`pdf-viewer-toolbar-button.tsx:62-63`).
openQuestions.changes: The toggle adds a close path to a control the modal Sheet already renders unreachable while open, duplicating the Sheet's own "Close thumbnails" button at `pdf-viewer-thumbnails.tsx:123-130`. The opener removes an attribute and one assertion, and leaves the desktop and mobile controls deliberately different in kind, which the file should then say.

Both disclosure triggers gate `aria-controls` on `open` rather than on panel presence, each carrying the same comment asserting the panel unmounts while closed, which is false under `mount="always"`; neither calls the exported `mountsEveryPanel` the mount primitive documents for exactly this decision and that Stepper already uses.

openQuestions.question: Does a hand-written multi-child skeleton carry its own `data-slot` root anchor, or is `placeholder` the family anchor?
openQuestions.axes: CONVENTIONS.md:102 §10.2 asks every new component for a stable `data-slot`. CONVENTIONS.md:39 §3.7 puts pagination in a hand-written family, and the factory the rest of that family uses (placeholder-skeleton.ts:79-81) emits no per-skeleton anchor, so a per-skeleton anchor on pagination alone would be the outlier rather than the norm.
openQuestions.changes: Anchoring widens S9 from pagination-skeleton.tsx to every hand-written count-keyed skeleton §3.7 names (heading, textarea, tabs, stepper, breadcrumb), most of which sit outside the B07 file list and would need their own scope. Declaring `placeholder` the family anchor closes B07-C12 as convention-conformant with a TSDoc note and no code change.

ruledOut.id: B07-C09 — the dropped part: "nothing in the block is focusable"
ruledOut.guard: packages/ui/src/components/code/code-block.tsx:154 `{copy && <CopyButton value={code} size="sm" className={cn(k.copy)} />}`, with the default set at :86 `copy = true,` and documented at :63-64 "/** Renders a CopyButton overlay. @defaultValue `true` */". A focusable button therefore sits inside `data-slot="code-block"` by default. What the traced part confirms is narrower and still holds: the CopyButton is a sibling of the scroll container (:142 `<div className={cn(k.block.content)}>`), not a descendant of it, so the scrollable region itself remains without a keyboard entry point.

ruledOut.guard: packages/ui/src/__tests__/components/pagination.test.tsx:13-19 — `it('pairs with an explicit PaginationSkeleton in loading trees', () => {` / `const { container } = renderUI(<PaginationSkeleton pages={5} />)` / `expect(bySlot(container, 'pagination')).not.toBeInTheDocument()` / `expect(allBySlot(container, 'placeholder')).toHaveLength(5)`. Only the narrower part is confirmed: the root `<div>` at pagination-skeleton.tsx:25 carries no `data-slot` of its own.

ruledOut.id: B07-C15 — the dropped part: that three tab stops is itself the defect
ruledOut.guard: packages/ui/src/hooks/a11y/use-a11y-roving.ts:776-780 — "Seats `tabIndex=0` on the resting item (see `activeSelector`, else the first item) and `-1` on the rest, keeps that invariant as the subtree mutates, and moves the `0` with focus on each arrow press. Leave off for widgets whose items already drive their own `tabIndex` (e.g. `Tab`'s `tabIndex={current?0:-1}`) or that must stay individually Tab-focusable (plain site-nav links)." The hook documents leaving the option off as a supported choice, and packages/ui/src/components/accordion/accordion-trigger.tsx:23-24 places the component under "the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern", which the file at accordion.tsx:100 also names for the container. No repository source establishes a single Tab stop as the accordion's requirement, and no test asserts one. What is confirmed is the prose-versus-code mismatch: two TSDoc sites say "roving tabindex" while accordion.tsx:94-96 seats none.

groups.cause: A caller-supplied value reaches a memo or a dependency array by identity, so whether the memo holds depends on how the caller spells its argument rather than on what the argument is.

A portalled panel's DOM node arrives a commit after the flag that opens it, so anything keyed on the flag alone — a one-shot effect, or a handler reading node-as-state — runs against a node that is not there yet.

openQuestions.question: When a status clears to `null` (or the hook is disabled) and then returns to the exact string last spoken, must it be spoken again?
openQuestions.axes: Whether an absent message is a state change worth resetting the baseline, or merely a gap in a continuing status. Weigh a reader who re-queries and lands on the same count — who hears nothing today — against a reader who watches a value flicker to null and back on every refetch, who would then hear the same sentence repeatedly.
openQuestions.changes: Reset-on-absent makes S2 a change inside the hook and covers every future caller that passes a nullable status. openQuestions.question: Q2 — Is the toast lifetime per toast, or one deadline for the stack?
openQuestions.axes: The queue is built for a stack-wide sweep (use-toast-queue.ts:52 snapshots every non-persistent toast and drains it head-first on one fire), while `ToastInput.duration` (types.ts:46) and `'timeout'` as "the toast's own lifetime running out" (types.ts:16) describe per-toast lifetimes. Only one of the two can be the contract.
openQuestions.changes: Per-toast means each toast carries its own deadline and the queue snapshots only the expired ones — the change reaches `use-toast-timer.ts` and `use-toast-queue.ts` and re-opens the WCAG 2.2.1 pause accounting, which today is one counter for one timer. Stack-wide means the arithmetic picks a deadline deliberately (the minimum remaining rather than the newest) and the per-toast field's TSDoc is the thing that is wrong — a much narrower diff confined to `toast.tsx:113`.

openQuestions.question: Q3 — Where does `null` stop collapsing to `undefined`: in `useControllable`, or inside the current cascade?
openQuestions.axes: `use-controllable.ts:34,55` fold `null` deliberately and say so ("Internally \"no value\" is always `undefined`"), and that hook backs every controlled component in the package. `CurrentContextValue.value: string | undefined` (current.ts:9-10) and the `contextValue === undefined` arm of `matchesCurrent` (current-content.tsx:63-64) are local to one primitive.
openQuestions.changes: Fixing the hook makes `null` distinguishable everywhere and puts every `useControllable` consumer in the blast radius, including the §7.2 binding cascade. Fixing the cascade keeps the diff inside `primitives/current` — `useCurrentState` stops routing `null` through the hook, the context value widens, and `matchesCurrent` grows a third arm — at the cost of one component knowing something the shared hook does not.

openQuestions.question: Q4 — In SidebarLayout, does only padding move to the `space` axis, or the desktop panel width too?
openQuestions.axes: `DensityToken` assigns padding and gap to `space` and text and icon to `size` (primitives/density/density.tsx:14-18); a rail's width is neither. The layout reads one token property for all four uses today.
openQuestions.changes: Padding-only flips one pinned assertion (sidebar.test.tsx:268-284) and leaves `k.panel`'s `size` variant untouched. Moving the width as well flips a second (sidebar.test.tsx:90-106) and renames the variant key in `layouts/sidebar/variants.ts:25-30`, which also decides whether the same question is owed to the other layouts that size furniture off the token.

openQuestions.question: Q5 — Does `providers/density` split its cascade-reading hook into its own `'use client'` module, or take the directive on the whole file?
openQuestions.axes: `DensityProvider` is server-renderable today precisely because the file carries no directive, and REFERENCE.md:31 protects the pattern of a directive-free host opening a density scope. `useDensityLevel` is a client-tier read and PROVIDERS.md:30 already says so.
openQuestions.changes: A split adds a file and a barrel line and keeps the provider server-renderable. A whole-file directive costs nothing for today's client-only callers but forecloses an RSC `<DensityProvider>`, which is the entry point the provider doc calls "the app-wide entry point for ambient density".

openQuestions.question: Q6 — For a modal Overlay with `backdrop={false}`, does the outside press dismiss, or is the combination refused?
openQuestions.axes: The `backdrop` TSDoc frames the flag as paint-only and independent of modality (overlay.tsx:78-86), while the dismissal comment assumes a modal overlay always has a backdrop to click (overlay.tsx:133-135). Second axis: the boundary. The dismissal ref is the full-viewport root, so "outside the panel" is inside the boundary unless the ref moves.
openQuestions.changes: Dismissing means `outsidePointer` keys on "no backdrop rendered" rather than `!modal`, and the boundary ref moves from the root to the panel — which also touches how a portalled child press is judged (`pressLandsInSurfaceOpenedWithin`). Refusing means the prop type ties `backdrop: false` to `modal: false`, closing the row with no behaviour change and no new test, and pushing the same question onto Sheet's re-exported `backdrop`.

verdicts.mechanism: packages/ui/src/utilities/format.ts:144 `if (spec.type === 'id') return (value) => formatId(value, spec)` — the `id` branch never reaches `Intl.NumberFormat`. packages/ui/src/utilities/format.ts:119-127: `const whole = Math.trunc(value)`; `const sign = whole < 0 ? '-' : ''`; `const digits = Math.abs(whole).toString()`; `const body = spec.pad ? digits.padStart(spec.pad, '0') : digits`; `return spec.prefix ? \`${spec.prefix}${spec.separator ?? groups.cause: The shared live-region write path in `announce` holds one module-scope node and mutates it inside a single task, so it neither notices that the node left the document nor gives the accessibility tree a rest state between two identical messages.

Three one-function helpers state a guarantee their implementation drops at one edge — no runtime freeze behind "frozen singletons", `undefined` doubling as the WeakMap miss sentinel, and the at-most-once flag set after the call can throw — and no shipped caller reaches any of the three edges.

steps.change: Rework the write path in `announce`: check the cached region is still connected before writing (re-create it when it is not), and give the clear and the set separate rest states so a repeated identical message is an observed change. Extend the existing test to drive a repeat message and a cleared body.
steps.order: First — B11-C03 carries the only medium severity in the scope and fires from a shipped default with no consumer wiring (a CopyButton pressed twice), and both rows sit in one 73-line file, so one change closes them together.
steps.seam: None of the §10.3 subjects is under this defect: `announce` is plain DOM plus `queueMicrotask`, and `__resetAnnouncer` (announcer.ts:66-73) is the teardown seam. If Q1 lands on a timer, the test must drive it through fake timers rather than a real delay.

openQuestions.question: Q1 — What timing does the live region need for a repeated identical message, and does the announcer own re-attachment or does the caller?
openQuestions.axes: Microtask (today) against a task boundary (`setTimeout`) or a frame; and re-create the detached region against leaving detachment to `__resetAnnouncer`. The second axis turns on whether any shipped surface is ever expected to clear `document.body`, which today none is.
openQuestions.changes: A task boundary makes S1 a timing change and forces fake timers in the test; keeping the microtask makes S1 a re-attachment change only and leaves B11-C03 as a recorded row. Choosing not to re-attach drops B11-C02 from S1 and leaves the row test-scoped.

openQuestions.question: Q2 — Does the product ship an RTL surface, now or on the roadmap?
openQuestions.axes: Ships or does not. The evidence today: no `rtl` in apps/admin, apps/places or the demos, and packages/ui/src/utilities/scrollbar-press.ts:16-17 already carries the RTL branch, so the intent to support it exists in code.
openQuestions.changes: If RTL ships, S2 rises above S1 in the order and the row's severity is medium, because the false positive blocks dismissal on every bordered scroller. If it does not, S2 stays a latent correction and its new test file is the only guard.

openQuestions.question: Q3 — Does the `id` formatter's contract cover non-finite input, or does the caller guard?
openQuestions.axes: The formatter handles NaN and Infinity itself, against the caller guarding before it calls (which is what the @remarks tells the caller to do for the numeric specs). A third axis: whether the two branches of `FormatSpec` are allowed to differ here at all.
openQuestions.changes: Handling it in the formatter makes S3 a change to `formatId` plus two test cases. Leaving it to the caller makes S3 a test-only change that pins the current strings, and B11-C13 becomes a documented divergence between the two branches rather than a defect.

openQuestions.question: Q4 — Between an extra and a slot of the same name, which wins, and should the clash be an error?
openQuestions.axes: Throw (extending the guard's documented set), let the slot win (assign extras first), or keep last-writer-wins as an unstated feature. No shipped kata exercises any of the three, so the decision is about future kata only.
openQuestions.changes: Throwing makes S4 a guard widening plus a test case and updates the `@throws` set. Slot-wins makes S4 a two-line reorder with no new error. Keeping today's order closes B11-C05 with no code change and leaves it recorded.

openQuestions.question: Q5 — How far does "best-effort" extend for `aria-labelledby`?
openQuestions.axes: Resolve the first ID in the list, join every resolved target's text (what the ARIA algorithm does), or hold the single-ID read and let the current fallback stand. Weigh against the helper's own disclaimer at accessible-name.ts:4-5 that it is not the full algorithm.
openQuestions.changes: Joining makes S5 a loop plus a test; first-ID-only makes it a `split` plus a test; holding closes B11-C01 with no code change and records the list case as out of scope.

openQuestions.question: Q6 — For the three unreached helper guarantees, harden the runtime or hold the rows as recorded?
openQuestions.axes: Cost of the change (all three are one or two lines) against the value of a guarantee no caller exercises; and whether the package wants runtime freezing at all, given `as const` is the house idiom and referential stability is the tested property.
openQuestions.changes: Hardening runs S6 as one commit with two new test files. Holding drops S6 entirely and leaves B11-C07, B11-C09 and B11-C10 as recorded-and-unreached rows; a middle outcome (harden `once` and `memoWeak`, hold the freeze) narrows S6's file set to the two utilities.

The imperative `announce` (packages/ui/src/core/announcer.ts:52) and the declarative `useA11yAnnouncements` (packages/ui/src/hooks/a11y/use-a11y-announcements.ts:39 `announce(message, { assertive })`) write through the same two module-scope regions with no coordination, so a component narrating a changing value and a one-off toast share one node and can overwrite each other mid-announcement. This is a cross-component seam no single file shows.
